docs.title: Distillery and Cafe
docs.text:
When compatible Distillery is enabled, all four fallback spirit definitions and recipes are hidden. Mixology uses genuine distilled vodka, tequila, rum and whiskey instead, including valid older Distillery bottles. Renaming a potion does not make it a spirit. Existing standalone bottles remain in inventories but cannot substitute for genuine integrated ingredients.

Wine integration requires capability 2 and the DISTILLERY_WINE recognizer. It accepts genuine non-distilled Wine or Champagne profiles, including valid legacy bottles, and rejects Cider, Beer, Mead, malformed profiles and renamed impostors. Spirit capability 1 remains supported: Sweet Vermouth, Negroni/Boulevardier, Manhattan, Americano, Dry Martini and Corpse Reviver No. 2 are hidden without wine support. Corpse Reviver No. 2 also follows Vermouth availability. Death in the Afternoon additionally requires capability 3 and the distillery:sparkling_wine qualifier: genuine Sparkling Wine still has the ordinary DISTILLERY_WINE identity, but its recorded secondary fermentation must validate. Ordinary Wine, renamed bottles and metadata-free previews cannot substitute. The integrated counts above assume capability 3; Death is omitted in standalone mode and with older integration.

When enabled Distillery lacks even the spirit Mixology capability, the alcoholic recipes and fallback spirits stay hidden. An administrator diagnostic asks for the matching update; the four non-alcoholic Mixology recipes still produce five named drinks. Cafe independently enables Coffee Liqueur, Espresso Martini, Black Russian, White Russian, Mudslide and B52. Standalone Rum does not require Cafe.

docs.title: Alcohol Strength
docs.text: Standalone Mixology does not add drunkenness behavior. With Distillery, mixed drinks retain diluted ABV and use the same Core quality for their lore, later crafting and quality-dependent alcohol effects. Retired brewing powers are not inherited, and mixed drinks cannot be fed back into distillation or used as genuine spirits.

docs.title: Alcohol servings and quality
docs.text:
Recipe previews show an Average alcohol estimate, calculated through the selected recipe and its linked source recipes. Both ABV and equivalent-40%-cl reflect ingredient amounts, intermediate volumes and the number of output drinks. Actual crafted drinks show their real values. Clicking a logical spirit such as Vodka opens its Distillery production preview; Back returns to your Mixology recipe. Editing that separate brewing preview does not silently change the parent recipe.

Spirit ingredient cards, including Rum, show the tint and brewing guidance of their linked Distillery production preview. They keep the recipe's required quantities. These are display previews; actual brewing and mixing still require genuine ingredients.

Drinks show their alcohol dose as the equivalent amount of a 40% spirit, for example 🪣Alcohol: 20% ABV · 4 cl, and one Quality row using Heirloom's existing dice and names. The displayed cl is actual liquid cl × ABV / 40: an 8 cl drink at 20% has a 4 cl equivalent dose. Mocktails show 0 cl. Plain juices and Soda Water have no alcohol row. This is alcohol dose, not the physical amount in the glass.

Brewing profiles also show ◾Sugar, ⚗Acid and ♣Tannins. Symbols touch their labels with no space: Alcohol uses cyan, Sugar cream, Acid yellow and Tannins green. Only the symbols receive these colors; labels retain the normal Heirloom theme.

Core quality controls the displayed quality, later crafting and quality-dependent alcohol effects. Station and ice bonuses improve this same quality without changing ABV or serving volume. Legacy beverages seed Core quality from their old alcohol quality only when Core quality is absent; an existing precise Core value is preserved.

One default liquid or squeezed-produce portion is 4 cl. Produced drinks remember their actual volume, so a liqueur made from two 4 cl liquids contains 8 cl. Gin, Aromatic Bitters and Absinthe infuse botanicals without adding juice; dry ingredients and ice add no modeled liquid. No item-definition volume fields are required.

Every mix uses the stored actual liquid volumes: batch alcohol is the sum of each input's volume × ABV / 100, final ABV is batch alcohol / total liquid × 100, and each output receives total liquid / output count. Mixing and splitting preserve the total equivalent alcohol dose; juice lowers ABV without removing alcohol. Fresh Juicer batches produce two 6 cl servings of actual juice; their actual volume contributes to later mixing, but juice itself has no alcohol row. Stored volume remains actual liquid volume and is never reinterpreted as equivalent cl. Missing legacy volume defaults to 4 cl actual volume, preserving the old ABV and quality; malformed explicit volume is rejected.

With Distillery, lore and intake use the same equivalent-alcohol conversion. The default meter holds 40 cl: a 10 cl dose fills one quarter before player sensitivity. The drunkenness readout uses a separate 0–4‰ game scale: /hld drunk shows ‰, while item lore continues to show equivalent cl. A 10 cl dose raises the default meter by 1‰ before sensitivity. Bare numbers in /hld setdrunk and /hld adddrunk retain their cl meaning; add an explicit ‰ suffix to use the game scale, for example /hld setdrunk Alex 1.2‰. Only presentation is rounded. Fractional amounts persist, and explicit administrator overrides remain effective. Distillery retains variable fermentation strength and emits standard 4 cl servings of actual liquid; its brewing-flow reference shows the current default extraction curve. Mixing conserves alcohol; distillation remains a game production mechanic. Standalone Mixology adds no drunkenness behavior.

docs.title: Included visuals and excluded content
docs.text:
The release uses player-head fruit and cocktail visuals, the supplied shaker body/lid textures, and vanilla bottle models for juices. Some named cocktails intentionally share approved head reuse; the recipe browser still shows each named result and its ingredients. No resource pack is required.

Dates and the deferred dishes are excluded from the release counts and buyer scope. The deferred dishes are Lemonade, Sticky Date Pudding, Mango Sticky Rice, Avocado Toast and the old standalone Orange Juice definition. Pure Orange Juice from the Juicer and Sparkling Lemonade remain active. The deferred editable owner-asset contracts remain gated. Nexo, ItemsAdder and CraftEngine provider packages are not included. No future visual package is required or included in this release.

docs.title: Admin operation
docs.text:
/hlo info reports the live item/tree counts and remaining owner-head count. /hlo reload validates editable files and swaps registrations transactionally. Editable resources live under plugins/HeirloomOrchard/; generated runtime files stay under its .runtime/ child and never overwrite the editable sources.

The current settings are in plugins/HeirloomOrchard/config.yml. Core handles the marketplace license, so a normal Voxel installation does not need an addon license key. warn-on-draft controls the notice about deferred owner assets without enabling that excluded content. Edit trees-orchard.json for fruit trees, crops-orchard.json for Pineapple, juice-produce-orchard.json for juice choices, and custom_items-orchard.json / recipes-orchard.json for item and recipe rules. Acquisition controls are described above. Run /hlo reload after valid content edits and inspect /hlo info.

Defaults are added without replacing administrator edits. Optional-addon changes refresh the selected content and browser entries. Existing ingredients keep their original identity and metadata through station recovery; cosmetic fruit heads and the shaker are not additional refundable items. Verify the physical shaker, Juicer, GUI and fruit harvests in a real client before reporting visual acceptance. Capture requirements are in the Mixology media brief.

docs.title: Animal Care
docs.text:
Give animals food, water, a roof and enough room. They handle everyday care themselves; brushing and treats are optional bonuses.

Start with a small herd you can get to know, then improve their home and choose promising breeding stock.

Open /hl → Animal Care for the short in-game guide.

docs.title: Your first farm
docs.text:
1. Choose a group from the table below. Leave room for each animal to move and rest.
  2. Add its forage and bedding. Keep them nearby with clear paths.
  3. Provide drinking water. Use still water or a water-filled cauldron. Leave a clear standing place right beside it.
  4. Build a roof. Give the barn an open entrance, enough headroom and space inside.
  5. Hold a brush. Item bubbles show what managed animals are doing. Sneak-brush one for details and a useful tip.
Animal Group Food in the habitat Bedding Products Cow 2 or more Grass blocks Hay or moss Milk, meat, leather Goat 2 or more Grass blocks Hay or moss Milk, meat Sheep 3 or more Grass blocks Hay or moss Milk, meat, wool Pig 2 or more Mud or muddy mangrove roots Hay or moss Meat Chicken 3 or more Planted crops on farmland Hay or moss Eggs, meat Frog 2 or more Firefly bushes Moss blocks or moss carpet Meat

Crowding counts all six livestock species together, including wild animals. Same-species companions satisfy company.

Dropped food does not replace these habitat blocks. Dairy animals also graze grass to refill milk, so leave grass available to regrow. No special trough or registered pen is needed.

Keep forage and bedding within sixteen horizontal blocks of where animals spend their time, with a clear route. They remember successful feeding spots, but still need to be able to reach them. Eating and drinking have quiet nearby sounds.

Wild animals use ordinary vanilla behaviour by default. Breed supported livestock with their usual food to get a managed youngster with a farm name. Name tags override that name. Frogspawn and thrown eggs do not track ancestry; server owners can change enrollment in the settings.

docs.title: Read the brush display
docs.text:
Brush normally to give an eligible bonus and show a short status display. Sneak-brush for the animal's name, mood and activity, five need bars, Yield / Quality, and known parents.

Beside the mood, look for what they are doing or want: Drinking, Looking for forage, or Would like brushing. Taking it easy means no care task is active. Hover that phrase for a short explanation; brushing and treat wishes are optional extra attention.

Each need uses an item icon and four coloured squares. Hover a bar for its percentage and one line of help. Food, water, rest and comfort fill as they improve. Company is green in the middle, red when lonely or crowded. A mixed crowd can be overcrowded and still lack companions of the same species. Crowding starts above ten other livestock within four blocks and builds gradually. Even at maximum density, crowding alone will not make a healthy animal distressed; spreading out helps it reach its best moods.

The product row shows an item and a yield multiplier. Food products also show quality dice; wool and leather use yield only. Hover a product for its permanent traits and any birth-quality bonus. Adult pigs also show one Pig Casing, a fixed Normal-quality drop without inherited traits. Comparisons use only the immediately previous inspection: a different animal of the same species, within 60 seconds.

A Barrier on a bubble means a resource or path is blocked. Hearts mean care finished. A tip appears when there is something useful to fix; an animal already drinking does not need another water reminder.

docs.title: Get to know the herd
docs.text:
Some animals love brushing; others prefer a treat. Offering their favourite food or preferred care reveals a little more about them. Hover their name in sneak-brush inspection to remember what they like. Pigs favour one of their usual vegetables, and chickens one of the common seeds; wheat-fed animals and frogs keep their familiar foods.

A wish is an optional invitation to spend a moment together. Brushing or giving a treat can fulfil it with a short happy reaction. A wish stays until fulfilled, even through sleep or a restart. There is no reaction deadline, and another wish waits at least one active day after completion. Wishes use the existing attention bonus and daily limits, and skipping one adds no penalty. Your habitat still handles everyday care.

Give pigs a patch of mud or muddy mangrove roots. When happy and relaxed, they can pause to play, kicking up little mud sprays with quiet squelches. They stop when they need care or sleep. The blocks stay intact.

docs.title: First birth → first harvest
docs.text:
1. Breed a pair and keep the youngster near companions. It prefers a reachable mother but can use other animals of its species.
  2. Sneak-brush different animals to compare product traits. Offspring inherit around the parental average, with some variation. Keep promising animals and compare several births.
  3. Let the youngster grow with good care. Genes set potential; care helps it produce better items.
  4. Milk adults, collect eggs or shear sheep. Turn the food into cheese, meat dishes or egg recipes.

Click Mother or Father to highlight a loaded, visible parent privately for ten seconds, within 64 blocks in the same world. An unavailable parent keeps its place in the ancestry.

x 1.50 means an average of one and a half items across repeated harvests: small bonuses carry forward. Dice show food quality. Wool and leather have no quality grade. Ordinary eggs with the same material, grade and metadata stack together; different colours, grades, names or food history can keep stacks separate.

docs.title: If something looks wrong
docs.text:
What you see What to change Looking for water Give the animal a clear standing place beside still water or a filled cauldron. Open gates and remove barriers at the edge. Looking for forage Use its habitat block from the table, with an open route. A pig needs mud; a chicken needs planted crops. Looking for shelter indoors Check the overhead roof, headroom and usable floor. Leave space beyond the entrance for animals to settle. Red company bar Add same-species companions if lonely; spread the herd out if crowded. More bedding cannot fix crowding. Good traits, poor products Check the need bars. Hitting causes temporary stress; it does not change genes.

At night animals rest until dawn. While sleeping, their needs do not fall and they stay quiet. A critically hungry or thirsty animal may need care first. Animals also seek cover in rain. Unloaded animals do not accumulate neglect.

For breeding details, livestock sales and server settings, see the Pasture overview.

docs.title: Heirloom Pasture
docs.text: This development candidate targets Java 25, Paper 26.2, and the matching Heirloom 2.10.1 build. The complete dairy loop uses built-in Minecraft player-head visuals for cheeses; Nexo, ItemsAdder, and CraftEngine visuals remain optional.

docs.title: Milk And Grazing
docs.text:
Adult cows, goats, and sheep hold milk charges. A managed animal recovers for four active minutes after its final charge is used, then seeks grass to replenish milk. Optional wishes, brushing, and hand-feeding cannot delay this recovery or manufacture milk. Only protected grass grazing restores dairy charges: mobGriefing, protection plugins, and cancellable block changes are respected. Unmanaged cows and goats retain their slow vanilla-inspired random grazing opportunity, and sheep retain native grazing. Milk refills one to three charges according to milk-yield genetics and current care.

Cold-climate cows provide Cold Cow milk, temperate cows provide vanilla milk buckets, and warm-climate cows provide Warm Cow milk; goats and sheep provide Goat Milk and Sheep Milk. The five menu choices are Temperate Cow, Cold Cow, Warm Cow, Goat and Sheep. These are real vanilla milk buckets: drinking one clears effects and returns the empty bucket. A natural animal's milk has Normal quality. Managed milk quality reflects its milk-quality trait and current care. Buckets retain their animal source, Contains: Milk, Vegetarian, and Gluten-Free metadata.

Vanilla milk is Temperate Cow milk. Both vanilla and legacy Dairy Milk use the existing Dairy affinities in new curd batches. Old Dairy Milk stacks remain accepted and unchanged; already-created cheese profiles retain their historical milk affinities.

Read the practical Animal Care guide for your first farm, brush readings and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Autonomous Animal Care
docs.text:
Build a comfortable home and animals take care of their basic needs themselves. Managed cows, goats, sheep, pigs, chickens, and frogs have nourishment, water, rest, company, and comfort needs. A suitable habitat keeps them healthy without compulsory daily chores. Brushing, hand-feeding, and occasional optional wishes reward extra attention with better production and better-developed offspring. Ignoring a wish never causes a failed need, starvation damage, or death.

Player-bred cows, goats, sheep, pigs, and chickens join care automatically. Naturally spawned animals remain wild by default. husbandry.manage-all-animals: true also enrolls supported animals at startup, spawn, or load; administrators can also enroll a target using /hlp debug husbandry enroll when debug helpers are enabled. Frogspawn and egg-hatch ancestry/enrollment are deferred; frogs and egg-hatched chicks enrolled through these management tools receive founder genetics.

docs.title: Build A Self-Sustaining Habitat
docs.text:
Use ordinary blocks, without registering pens or placing special furniture:

Species Forage Comfort and enrichment Cow Grass blocks Hay or moss bedding Goat Grass blocks Hay or moss bedding Sheep Grass blocks Hay or moss bedding Pig Mud or muddy mangrove roots Hay or moss bedding Chicken A planted crop over farmland Hay or moss bedding Frog Firefly bushes Moss blocks or moss carpet

Provide still water sources or non-empty water cauldrons with a clear standing edge, accessible roofs, and same-species company. Drinking starts only close to the actual resource; a nearby bowl behind a wall does not count. Ordinary forage, drinking, and enrichment are non-destructive; milk regeneration still consumes grass through the protected dairy system. Young animals prefer an accessible known mother; if she is missing or unreachable they can keep company with another animal of the same species. This never erases ancestry.

Food and water reserves last ten active minutes. Animals act before reserves run out and remain with an activity until satisfied. At night they seek cover and rest for the entire night. On reaching safe cover, a sleeping animal can make one short move two blocks farther beneath a continuous roof. This helps it settle inside a barn instead of just under the entrance. The move needs a reachable, unclaimed spot; a blocked path leaves the current safe cover available immediately. If the first decision runs out of time, the animal can wait briefly under that cover for at most two fresh attempts, bounded to 30 ticks, before settling there. Animals already settled inside keep their resting place. Resting animals are quiet, with floating Zs drifting up from their face; waking or interruption restores their previous sound setting. Sleeping preserves food, water, company, comfort and attention; rest restores energy. Crowding remains visible and caps mood while sleeping. Exhausted animals can also nap during the day. Missing bedding reduces comfort but does not prevent sleep. If cover is unreachable, safe outdoor rest is a fallback.

Managed goats with a current Happy, Delighted, or Thriving mood do not ram, including during the day or while meeting other needs. This uses the visible mood, including any overcrowding reduction. Rest and shelter routines also pause ramming at lower moods while they control movement. Outside those routines, goats below Happy retain their ordinary ramming behaviour. Their other AI remains active. A scoped native ram guard also prevents happy goats from causing ram damage or knockback, including when a target is already in its damage cooldown.

Exposed animals seek shelter in actual rain and leave when the storm clears; dry biomes do not produce false rain complaints. Panic, temptation, breeding, transport, and player control take precedence. Interrupted animals can resume their previous destination. During a rainy night, critically hungry or thirsty animals can use reachable covered resources before returning to rest. Slabs, stairs, and carpets use their actual surface height; gates and entrances must still allow the animal through.

Shelter and company searches reach sixteen horizontal blocks; water, forage, and comfort searches reach eight, with eight blocks of vertical allowance. Keep paths, gateways, and entrances wide enough for the animal. No search loads distant chunks. Nearby animals share discovered places, and changed or blocked places are rechecked. Server work waiting in a queue is never treated as poor care. Newly discovered shortages receive a one-active-minute grace period. Unloaded or inactive time does not accumulate neglect.

Each managed animal has a lasting preference for brushing or treats. Successful care can reveal that preference; pigs and chickens can also have different favourite foods from their usual common foods. Hover the animal's name in sneak-brush inspection to remember discoveries. These preferences belong to the animal and remain through restarts; they are separate from inherited production traits. Optional wishes vary between eligible brushing and feeding and remain until fulfilled, including through sleep, urgent care, chunk unloads and restarts. The next wish waits at least one active day after completion. Completing one gives a short acknowledgement and the existing attention reward, subject to its normal daily limits. Skipping wishes adds no penalty.

Happy, relaxed pigs already standing on mud or muddy mangrove roots occasionally take a short playful pause, with small directional mud sprays and quiet squelches. They immediately yield to needs, sleep or player interaction. Mud play does not damage blocks or change production, and it does not search for a destination. The ambient-effects setting controls its particles and sounds.

Give livestock room to spread out. More than ten other supported animals within four horizontal blocks and two vertical blocks gradually lowers comfort, visible mood, and current production; the crowding pressure reaches its maximum at twenty neighbors. Other species and wild animals count, but players and animals on distant floors do not. A roof or bedding cannot cancel overcrowding. The brush reports “Overcrowded: needs more space”; thinning or spreading the herd removes the mood cap and lets comfort recover normally. Brief clusters have a small effect. Sustained maximum crowding limits comfort to 70% and caps an otherwise healthy animal at Happy; crowding alone does not make it Distressed. Crowding never changes inherited traits or adds hit stress.

Adult pigs also show one Pig Casing in their product row. This fixed drop has Normal quality and no inherited casing traits. Adult player harvests require meat drops and doMobLoot to be enabled; humane sales also include one casing.

Ordinary single-source eggs and meat keep their vanilla names and omit redundant “Contains” lore. Their dietary and ingredient metadata remains available to recipes and Food Facts. Mixed foods, custom items and milk retain their appropriate source labels.

docs.title: Animal Care Guide And Brush Lens
docs.text:
Open the main Heirloom hub with /hl and select Animal Care. Hold a brush for a private husbandry lens: the nearest twenty-four managed animals within twelve blocks that the player has line of sight to and can see show contextual item bubbles. Icons are centered above the animal and periodically realigned as it moves. Each bubble is private to its brush-holding player and never changes the animal's real passenger list. Labels distinguish looking for a resource, walking toward it, using it, pausing, and finding no reachable resource nearby. A Barrier marks an actual blocked action; waiting for a search budget does not. A door represents shelter and rest. Successful care briefly shows the same contextual item with hearts.

With husbandry.ambient-effects enabled, small particles accompany actual foraging, drinking, and bedding use: grass or mud flecks, crop crumbs, water splashes, and occasional bedding flecks while resting. They use the resource the animal has reached and stop during searching, travel, or interruption. Bursts contain only two or three particles, shown to at most eight viewers within sixteen blocks.

Brush normally for care and a ten-second status display. A compact heading gives mood and activity. Native Minecraft item icons identify food (wheat), water (water bucket), rest/shelter (oak door), company (lead), and comfort (feather), each beside four coloured squares. Food, water, rest, and comfort fill as those needs are met. Company is green in the middle and red at the lonely or crowded ends, without extra labels between the bars. Hover a need for its percentage and a short explanation. A mixed crowd can still lack same-species company. The icons need no resource pack and the display uses the warm Heirloom palette. Wild identifies unmanaged animals.

Brushing and treats add optional attention bonuses. A good habitat handles everyday care without daily player attention. Repeated brushing refreshes information without repeatedly awarding care or consuming durability. At most one optional wish appears per active Minecraft day; already completed care is not requested again. Wishes stay until fulfilled. Feeding can still satisfy real hunger between bonus rewards. Sleeping preserves attention.

Managed animals receive stable species-specific farm names at enrollment or birth; name tags take priority. Sneak-brush to see the name, mood and activity, five need bars, one Yield / Quality product row, and known parents. Food products show their item icon, yield multiplier and quality dice (⚀–⚅). Wool and leather show yield only. Hover a product for exact values, permanent breeding traits, and the separate birth-quality bonus. The same hover compares traits with the immediately previous inspection, if it was a different animal of the same species within 60 seconds. Logging out or changing worlds clears the comparison. Hover the name for its stable identity.

At most one short tip suggests a useful change, such as opening a route to water or adding more space. An animal already satisfying its need does not repeat that advice.

Click a known parent's link in the inspection to highlight that parent privately for ten seconds. Links last 60 seconds and work only for the inspecting player while the parent is loaded, visible to that player, and within 64 blocks in the same world. Clicking another parent replaces the previous highlight. This does not load distant chunks or change anyone else's view.

Inspection does not spend brush durability, advance care, or award attention. A first inspection can record stable founder genes; it does not enroll a wild animal or reroll an existing genome. The breeder privately receives newborn trait differences from the parental average after a successful birth. A good pairing can still produce an individual below average; compare several generations.

docs.title: First Farm, First Birth, First Harvest
docs.text:
1. Start with two cows, goats, pigs or frogs, or three sheep or chickens of the same species and provide their forage, accessible still water, shelter, bedding or enrichment, and room to move. Use the Animal Care guide for that species.
  2. Feed the pair their normal breeding food. Directly bred supported newborns become managed even when their parents are wild. Keep the youngster near accessible company as it grows.
  3. Hold a brush to see what a managed animal needs. Sneak-brush two animals to compare permanent traits; ordinary brushing is an optional bonus. Improve the habitat when a resource is blocked.
  4. Harvest milk or eggs, shear sheep, or confirm a livestock sale. Better genes and current care improve the actual output. Use the harvest in normal Heirloom recipes, including curds and cheese.

docs.title: Livestock Genetics
docs.text:
Each animal has separate yield ratings for its products and quality ratings for food products. Wool and leather use yield only:

Species Product traits Cow Milk, meat, leather Goat Milk, meat Sheep Milk, meat, wool Pig Meat Chicken Eggs, meat Frog Meat

Ratings range from 0 to 100. A directly bred offspring inherits the average of each parent's genes, with up to ten points of variation in either direction. Both parent identities are retained. Genomes are generated once and never rerolled by unloading or restarting. Existing managed animals start with neutral ratings of 50; previously unrecorded founders have stable ratings between 35 and 65. Merely recording a founder for breeding does not enroll the parent into care.

Sustained parental care during the previous active day gives offspring a separate, permanent quality bonus of up to five percentage points. Unknown history adds no bonus. This birth bonus is excluded from inherited gene calculations, so it cannot repeatedly compound as genetic potential.

Healthy habitats provide worthwhile production. Good breeding and extra attention let animals express more of their potential, up to three times the base yield. Current care still matters for animals with excellent genes. Milk, eggs, sheared wool, edible kill drops, leather, and livestock sales use the same yield rules. Wool and leather receive no quality metadata or lore. Feathers, wool from kills, Pig Casings, and experience retain their existing rules. Fractional rewards accumulate across repeated harvests; sale and slaughter rounding is stable. For example, a 1.6× egg yield carries the unused fraction forward; over five otherwise identical harvests, five base eggs become eight. Player and dispenser shearing share the same wool rules. Existing saved wool/leather quality genes remain readable but have no gameplay effect. Already-generated items are not rewritten. Sale rewards are fixed when quoted until that quote expires.

Ordinary eggs use the centre of their visible six-tier quality grade and a stable dietary-tag order. Same-material, same-grade eggs with matching metadata can stack; recipes use that grade centre. Existing eggs normalize on inventory touches without changing authored names, custom items, unrelated metadata or historical food provenance. Different evidence remains a real stack distinction, and occupied inventory slots are not forcibly repacked.

Animal brushing uses the normal hand swing. Minecraft's native archaeology sweep is block-only.

A successful nonlethal player hit shows Stressed and adds an 8 percentage-point production-care penalty, capped at 40%. The remaining penalty recovers over 2,400 active ticks while all five needs are at least 40%; poor conditions or inactive time pause recovery, and a further hit restarts the recovery period. Cancelled, zero-damage, and lethal hits add no penalty. Stress never changes genes or the parental care history used for birth bonuses. Nearby same-species managed witnesses with line of sight show Startled and briefly flee without losing permanent mood. Goat husbandry adds Raw Goat Meat, Cooked Goat Meat, and Minced Goat; the Cutting Board yields one mince and the Farmhouse Press yields two. Horses, dogs, and hatch ancestry are future additions, not supported breeding paths in this version.

Use a Gold Nugget on a managed adult for a five-second sale quote. Repeat to confirm. The nugget is reusable, and the first interaction shows Click to sell for meat above the animal. On confirmation, the animal pauses and fades where client support allows during a two-second sale animation. Its Looting-0 equivalent drops then go directly to the player, overflow is placed motionless at their feet, and the player receives 1–3 XP. The public cancellable PastureLivestockSaleEvent lets protection or economy plugins alter drops and XP or stop the sale. WorldGuard animal-harm permission is checked before the quote, confirmation, and completion; allowing interaction alone does not permit a sale. Protection changes or disabling sales during the animation restore the animal. The event also exposes immutable per-product yield and quality snapshots; its original constructor and legacy integer multiplier remain compatible. The fade uses client-only packets and never joins either entity to a real scoreboard team; incompatible viewers fall back to particles.

docs.title: Experimental Cheesemaking
docs.text:
Boil exactly three freely mixed milk pails into one Fresh Curds, three whey, and three returned buckets. The curds remember the milk blend. Treatments then move hidden affinities toward different cheeses: acid strongly suggests Paneer, a second boil plus hot water suggests Mozzarella, washing with water suggests Gouda, and cooking with whey suggests Halloumi. Salt and brine influence several styles. Applying the same treatment twice is rejected rather than silently consuming ingredients.

Mix treated curds into one Prepared Cheese. The Farmhouse Press immediately resolves a Feta-leading batch; every other batch becomes one unique, unstackable Young Cheese Wheel. Acid-set Paneer, stretched Mozzarella, and whey-cooked Halloumi instead finish fresh without aging. Every valid route produces its closest real cheese; there is no generic failure cheese.

Whey is a useful secondary ingredient rather than waste. Cook curds in whey for Halloumi, reheat three whey with lemon or vinegar for fresh Ricotta, or slowly reduce three whey with Heavy Cream for Brunost. Ricotta and Brunost are direct fresh finishes outside the affinity competition, pressing, and aging systems.

One of the 16 affinity cheeses may be consumed as culture. It adds affinity toward its own style. A matching winning style yields two finished cheeses, exactly once; a culture that loses yields one. Prepared Feta remains one intermediate and becomes two only when the matching cultured batch is pressed. Curds, prepared cheese and young wheels show their developing style and one actionable next step. Finished cheese keeps its provenance without development instructions. Intermediates borrow the current leader's provider visual or player-head fallback while keeping their generic identity and full process data.

docs.title: Pasture Cheeses Preview
docs.text:
Open /hl → Pasture Cheeses, /hlp menu or /hlp cheese. The catalog covers all 18 cheeses: 16 affinity previews plus the actual Ricotta and Brunost whey recipes. Animal Care remains a separate guide. Select a cheese to open its starting method, then experiment without consuming any items.

Left-click any of the three animal heads to choose a milk source; right-click cycles the five sources. Repeated and mixed sources work. Treatment and finish controls use the same transitions as production. Settings use the drink preview's controls: left-click next, right-click previous. The finish selector describes either a fresh finish in the Boiling Pot or preparation in the Mixing Bowl; the separate press icon explains collection or moving the young wheel to the rack. The supplementary ingredients follow the active recipes, including available Lemon or Vinegar. A matching culture updates the finished quantity. Ricotta and Brunost use their normal recipe screens without unrelated culture or cellar controls.

Slot Control 10, 19, 28 Independent milk selectors 11, 20, 29 Additional ingredients and quantities 16 Result and finished quantity 21 Milk to Fresh Curds, with whey and bucket returns 22 No treatment, second boil, water wash, or both 23 Acid-set, stretch, whey-cook, salt-and-press, or brine-and-press 24 Press step, where applicable 25 Aging a young wheel 31 Climate while aging 32 Nearby composter for eligible Casu Martzu batches while aging 33 Optional culture, consumed once 34 Reset to the selected cheese's original method 36/37 Back/Forward 43/44 Previous/Next Page

Aging choices are 0, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 days. Exact catalog durations are retained. The aging control uses the cheese lore's typography, for example ⏳Aging: 3 days · (1h). At zero age a pressed non-Feta batch is still a young wheel; it cannot finish until at least one day. Hidden climate and composter selections are remembered but do not affect the result. Changes refresh the current screen; Back returns to the same catalog page.

Preview provenance is explicitly simulated. Calculations assume Normal ingredients, successful station completion and no player mastery. Current station defaults produce Good quality; the preview uses production quality rules. Preview icons cannot be taken or used as cheese ingredients. Clicking an exact affinity cheese in another recipe opens its complete production preview; Any Cheese opens this catalog.

docs.title: Cheese Lore
docs.text:
Real cheeses and simulated previews share restrained colored symbols and one Core quality row. For example, an actual aged cow-milk cheese can show:

🪣Milk: Cow
♨Method: Salted · Pressed
⏳Aged: 3 days · (1h)
Cellar: Cool · Normal humidity
Quality: ⚂ Good

Milk blends show proportions such as 2 Sheep · 1 Goat; longer lines wrap without losing colors. Culture appears only when used. Finished cheese shows age and cellar only when recorded during production, never reconstructed from a suggested method. Completion stores the real age and climate separately from active rack state. Old validated items refresh when exposed; there is no stored-world scan. Items without a batch record, including Ricotta and Brunost, show known identity and quality without invented milk ancestry. Administrator names, formatted notes and custom lore remain intact. Updating unchanged default filler does not replace edited item descriptions. Curds and wheels keep a useful next step; ready wheels explain removal, and finished Feta never suggests further aging.

The diagram is generated from the same versioned affinity catalog used by runtime scoring, lore, and the recipe browser. It contains no hidden scores and is checked for all sixteen routes during wiki generation.

docs.title: Suggested Methods
docs.text:
These are reliable traditional routes generated from the same affinity definitions used by gameplay. They are suggestions, not locked recipes: unconventional blends and other cow-milk Mozzarella remain valid.

Cheese Suggested method Mozzarella Cold Cow milk; second-boil; hot-water stretch; salt; finish fresh. Paneer Warm Cow milk; acid-set with lemon or vinegar; finish fresh. Halloumi Two Goat and one Sheep milk; second-boil in whey; salt; finish fresh. Feta Two Sheep and one Goat milk; brine; press and collect immediately. Cheddar Temperate Cow milk; salt; press; age 2–4 days in a cool or temperate cellar. Parmesan-style Temperate Cow milk; second-boil; brine; press; age at least 6 days in a dry cellar. Brie Temperate Cow milk; salt; press; age 1–2 days in a cool humid cellar. Roquefort-style Blue Sheep milk; salt; press; age 4–6 days in a cool humid cellar. Gouda Temperate Cow milk; water-wash; brine; press; age 2–4 days in a temperate cellar. Emmental Warm Cow milk; salt; press; age 2–4 days in a warm cellar. Manchego Sheep milk; salt; press; age 4–6 days in a dry cellar. Provolone-style Temperate Cow milk; second-boil; salt; press; age 2–4 days in a warm dry cellar. Crottin-style Goat Cheese Goat milk; salt; press; age 1–2 days in a cool dry cellar. Gorgonzola-style Blue Temperate Cow milk; salt; press; age 4–6 days in a cool humid cellar. Maroilles-style Washed Rind Temperate Cow milk; brine; press; age 2–4 days in a temperate humid cellar. Casu Martzu Sheep milk; salt; press; age six warm days beside a level 6+ composter.

The in-game catalog opens these methods as editable production previews. Actual station recipes remain available; the old non-craftable suggested-recipe entries are replaced by production links.

docs.title: Farmhouse Press
docs.text:
Build the exact press geometry:

front/output <- DISPENSER (facing outward) <- HOPPER (facing into dispenser)
                SCAFFOLDING

The press has no GUI, accessible inventory, or molds. Put exact ingredients through the rear hopper. They appear in the world during the 15-second process and progressively reveal the result from the dispenser mouth. Cheese compresses, meat grinds, sausages and pasta extrude, and oil presses with distinct motion. The completed result stays visible at the dispenser mouth like other workstation results. Punch the press to release it 0.72 blocks from the dispenser center with a small outward-only horizontal velocity and no upward or backward motion, so it cannot reach the rear hopper. Reserved work survives normal restarts.

docs.title: Meat, Sausages, Pasta, And Oil
docs.text:
An adult pig killed directly by a player drops exactly one Pig Casings when doMobLoot is enabled. Looting never multiplies it. Beef, pork, mutton, and Pasture Goat Meat can be hand-minced one at a time on the Cutting Board, or ground in the Farmhouse Press for two typed portions. Legacy generic Minced Meat remains valid for ordinary Core recipes and Plain Links.

The press stuffs and finishes each sausage batch directly; there are no separate raw-link items:

Sausage Press ingredients Plain Links 2 any minced meat, Salt, Pig Casings Garlic Pork Sausage 2 Minced Pork, Garlic, Salt, Pig Casings Swedish Potato Sausage Minced Pork, Minced Beef, Potato, Onion, Salt, Pig Casings Cheese Sausage Minced Pork, Minced Beef, any cheese, Salt, Pig Casings

Plain Links plus Bread become a Hot Dog in the Frying Pan. Quality, meat and dairy provenance, dietary properties, and Contains metadata survive every stage. The press also turns one Dough into two Dry Pasta, or the existing sunflower/corn oil inputs into two Cooking Oil; the older Cutting Board and Mixing Bowl methods remain available at their original one-item yields.

Garlic is entirely Pasture-owned and grows as a four-stage temperate Allium with Onion-like timing, harvest, replanting, and Fortune behavior. It appears in temperate packets, suitable grass biomes, and village farm loot at roughly sixty percent of Onion's weight.

Bake Garlic Bread in the Oven with Bread, Garlic, and either Butter or Cooking Oil; the oil method is the vegan alternative. Adult frogs killed directly by players drop one Raw Frog Legs when doMobLoot is enabled. French Fried Frog Legs are available only while Heirloom Orchard is installed, because Orchard owns Lemon. Fry Raw Frog Legs with a Bag of Flour, Butter, and Lemon in the Frying Pan. Looting does not multiply guaranteed Pasture animal drops such as Pig Casings. Managed-animal meat genetics and care improve frog and goat meat. Casings retain their existing yield; leather has its own yield trait.

docs.title: Continuous Aging Rack
docs.text:
A normal 27-slot barrel directly on scaffolding is an Aging Rack. It keeps its vanilla inventory and has no display entity or polling task. Every valid rack ages continuously in every climate. One aging day is 20 real minutes, and exact hidden epoch timestamps count eligible offline time.

Opening the barrel reconciles age, cumulative cool/temperate/warm and dry/normal/humid exposure, visuals, and exactly one owned lore section; it never finishes a wheel. Before one day, removing a wheel pauses it with progress preserved. At or after one day, player removal resolves the highest aged-cheese affinity. Breaking the supporting scaffolding pauses wheels rather than resolving them, and hopper automation remains blocked.

The dominant recorded exposure influences the result but never prevents aging, so no cheese requires multiple cellars. Finished lore records milk blend, treatments, culture, cellar history, and readable age such as ⏳Aged: 2.4 days · (48m). Young wheels have unique IDs and stack size one; two matching cultured outputs from the same batch share provenance and can stack together.

docs.title: Casu Martzu
docs.text:
Casu Martzu is a gated experimental route rather than a new mold or culture. Start with exactly three Sheep Milk pails, salt and press the wheel, then age it for six qualifying days in a warm rack with a composter at level 6 or higher directly north, east, south, or west of the barrel. Ordinary aging continues whenever those conditions are absent, but only qualifying exposure advances this route, and extra composters never accelerate it. Removing the wheel early resolves the closest ordinary cheese.

The wheel gradually reports disturbed rind, tracks, and movement before it becomes ready. Casu Martzu restores 8 food points and 5 saturation, always gives Nausea I for eight seconds, and has a 20% chance to give Hunger I for ten seconds. Its provenance contains Milk and Cheese-Fly Larvae; it is Gluten-Free but neither Vegan nor Vegetarian. Eating it for the first time awards the hidden challenge The Rind Is Moving.

docs.title: Compatibility, Debugging, And Attribution
docs.text:
All finished cheeses carry the CHEESE tag for compatible Core recipes. Optional farmer and shepherd starter trades are controlled by dairy.starter-trades.enabled. The player cheese menu requires heirloom.pasture.use; disabling dairy removes its previews and production links. Reloads replace the immutable preset index and bounded 256-entry calculation cache transactionally. Failed reloads retain the previous working generation; warm menu interactions do not rebuild the catalog.

All four husbandry switches apply on a successful /heirloom reload: enabled, ambient-effects, sell-for-meat, and manage-all-animals. Failed reloads retain the previous working configuration and runtime. Disabling automatic enrollment preserves already managed animals and their care, genetics, ancestry, stress, and fractional production. Disabling husbandry pauses that runtime and retains its stored animal data. Disabling sales cancels active animations and restores the animals.

The legacy dairy.enabled switch is a broad Pasture content gate: it controls dairy, cheese, and meat-processing items and recipes, plus their associated runtimes. It does not disable independent husbandry care. Use husbandry.enabled for that.

When debug.enabled is true, admins with heirloom.pasture.debug can use /hlp debug give <item-id> [amount], /hlp debug charge [true|false], /hlp debug press ready, /hlp debug rack inspect, /hlp debug rack advance <seconds>, and /hlp debug husbandry <enroll|inspect|mood> [tier].

See head-attribution-pasture.yml for Minecraft-Heads attribution and reserved textures.

docs.title: Village Trades
docs.text:
Village Trades is a Heirloom addon for making equipment, remedies and arrows at workstations. MMOItems supplies the finished items, their stats, sockets and abilities. MythicLib supplies the native skills and mana integration.

Unpublished candidate

These pages describe 1.0.0-rc.1, prepared for local review. A publicly supported minimum Core version is pending. Use the exact paired Core and addon builds in the candidate manifest. This page does not announce a release.

docs.title: The workshop
docs.text:
• Smithery: craft a cold equipment blank, heat it in the Oven, work it on an anvil, reheat as needed and quench it. Workmanship determines the finished grade.
  • Woodworking: place logs and fittings on a Fletching Table, shape the wood with a hatchet, then finish it with Honeycomb. Fittings stay beside the work until finishing.
  • Apothecary: cultivate herbs and use the Boiling Pot and Mixing Bowl for health, mana and damage-bonus preparations.
  • Fletching: combine a head, shaft and fletching on the bench. An optional Lingering Potion adds its native tipped-arrow effects.

The collection includes equipment for Steel and Mithral progression, native socket runes, an upgrade compound and a Repair Kit. The reference lists the current products and counts directly from the candidate catalogue. Workmanship variants and internal tongs appearances are not extra products.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Server owners should follow Setup, including mana and resource-pack configuration. Players can follow Survival progression from the bootstrap tools to their first equipment and herbs. Mithral deposits must first be placed by an operator; this candidate has no natural ore generation.

The target is Paper 26.2 with Java 25. Heirloom, MMOItems and MythicLib are required; other Heirloom addons are optional. The included pack is optional for joining, but players must accept it for woodworking. Optional PacketEvents 2.13.0 also enables custom nocked/flying arrow views and private tutorial scenes.

Automated checks and player confirmation are recorded separately in the candidate's docs/RELEASE-CANDIDATE.md. Inspect its exact build hashes before applying those results to an installation.

docs.title: Definitions and ownership
docs.text:
catalog.json in the candidate archive lists every public provider reference, exact workstation recipe, native preparation grid, crop and deposit. The in-game recipe browser uses the server's installed definitions and available providers. Do not substitute a renamed vanilla item for an exact MMOItems identity.

Provider names normalize, but provider-specific type/item IDs preserve case. Finished equipment, durability, lore, effects, sockets and upgrades remain native MMOItems data. Heirloom owns station work, grading and the persisted unfinished workpieces. Displays are projections of saved work, not extra refundable items.

docs.title: Operator commands
docs.text:
Command Use /vtrades help Workshop instructions. /vtrades status Inspect workshop status. /vtrades integrations Report current native integration modes; it is not an acceptance test. /hl deposits place VT_MITHRAL_DEPOSIT Register a valid bottom Stone Slab as a deposit. /hl deposits inspect Read remaining cycles and replenishment status. /hl deposits remove Remove registration without removing the slab; pending rewards must resolve first.

Testing kits and effect auditions are operator tools. The addon declares village-trades.kit and village-trades.debug, both operator-only by default. Ordinary survival progression does not depend on kits. The deposit commands use Core's administrative permission checks.

docs.title: Files to customize
docs.text:
Server path Content plugins/HeirloomVillageTrades/config.yml Workshop controls, balance and pack identity. plugins/HeirloomVillageTrades/recipes-village-trades.json Workstation recipe definitions and outputs. plugins/HeirloomVillageTrades/patterns.yml Smithing patterns. plugins/HeirloomVillageTrades/crops-village-trades.json Cultivatable herbs. plugins/HeirloomVillageTrades/acquisition-village-trades.json Discovery routes. plugins/HeirloomVillageTrades/deposits-village-trades.json Deposit yields, appearance and replenishment. plugins/Heirloom/custom_items-village-trades.json Provider-item catalogue declarations. plugins/MMOItems/item/*.yml Native item templates merged from supplied fragments. plugins/MythicLib/script/village_trades.yml and skill/village_trades.yml Native skill definitions.

workshop.json is runtime state, not a configuration template. Never replace it with a default or clear paid work to bypass a failed reload. Preserve it alongside worlds and inventories. Setup covers reload order and rollback.

docs.title: Village Trades setup
docs.text:
Candidate setup only

This guide describes unpublished 1.0.0-rc.1. The public minimum Core version is pending. Install the candidate's exact paired Core and addon jars, verified against manifest.yml; an older Core with the same version label is not sufficient.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Use Paper 26.2 and Java 25. Obtain MMOItems and MythicLib separately from their publishers. The inspected provider builds are MMOItems 6.10.1-SNAPSHOT and MythicLib 1.7.1-SNAPSHOT; their exact hashes are in the archive's docs/INSTALL.md. A matching snapshot label alone does not identify a tested binary.

Other Heirloom addons are optional. The native skills do not require MythicMobs. Optional PacketEvents 2.13.0 supplies custom nocked/flying arrow views and private tutorial scenes. Without it, arrow mechanics still work with native visuals.

docs.title: Install on a test copy first
docs.text:
1. Stop the server and make a consistent backup of its world, inventories, jars, provider settings, resource pack and runtime journals.
  2. Install the paired Core and compatible providers. Start them once to create their default configuration, then stop before merging Village Trades content.
  3. From the extracted candidate folder, preview the merge helper's changes: python3 tools/install.py --server /absolute/server. The helper needs Python 3 and PyYAML 6 on macOS/Linux. It does not install jars.
  4. Apply with the same command plus --apply. It backs up destination files, rejects conflicting keys and checks that the server is stopped. On Windows, use the manual merge instructions and destination table in the archive.
  5. Add the matching Village Trades jar to plugins/, configure mana and pack delivery below, then restart. Remove a superseded copy of the same addon jar so two versions cannot load together.

Never replace a complete MMOItems or MythicLib YAML file with a fragment. Merge the supplied root definitions into their corresponding files and preserve unrelated content. Keep the helper, fragments and defaults in their supplied relative directories. Do not copy a default over workshop.json.

The helper's backup is a configuration backup. It does not replace the complete world/player/journal backup needed to recover gameplay state. Unknown or pending transactions need investigation, not deletion to force the installer through.

docs.title: Mana
docs.text:
Preserve the server's existing configured mana provider. For a standalone setup without another mana system, edit these keys in the existing MythicLib files:

# plugins/MythicLib/config.yml
mana-plugin: MYTHICLIB

# plugins/MythicLib/stats.yml, inside its existing base-stat-value mapping
base-stat-value:
  MAX_MANA: 100
  MANA_REGENERATION: 1

Preserve other base stats. The helper diagnoses this choice without changing it. After restart, verify an actual staff cast and Mana Potion restoration. A configured value or present jar is not proof that the provider enabled.

docs.title: Resource pack
docs.text:
Serve resourcepack/Village-Trades-resourcepack.zip through a direct ZIP URL. Use its generated SHA-1 from resourcepack/manifest.json in server.properties's resource-pack-sha1. Set resource-pack to the direct URL. Do not serve the server directory or reuse an old hash for changed bytes.

Players may join with require-resource-pack=false, but woodworking requires acceptance. Keep server.properties's resource-pack-id equal to woodworking.resource-pack-id in plugins/HeirloomVillageTrades/config.yml. The supplied UUID is c86733c5-53a1-4907-803f-c3bda293d419; if changing it, update both settings. An accepted pack with a mismatched UUID will not unlock woodworking. MMOItems does not build or distribute the pack.

docs.title: First checks and later updates
docs.text:
Check startup for missing VT_ references, open the recipe browser and follow the first survival steps. Use /vtrades integrations to inspect native integration modes. A favorable diagnostic is not a gameplay acceptance result.

For item-template changes, run /mi reload followed by /hl reload. Restart for scripts, workshop settings or jar changes. Never use Bukkit /reload. Existing inventory items retain their saved provider data; a template reload does not regenerate them.

The tested optional baseline includes mcMMO 2.3.002 and MythicMobs 5.13.0. Current TNT splash preserves shooter ownership and passes per-target damage cancellation; it is not disabled merely because those plugins are installed. Validate your own region, faction and combat plugins. Homing is not a universal party/faction filter, and unknown mcMMO versions use the conservative native recovery path.

Keep the matched jars, manifest and acceptance receipt together. For rollback or removal, follow the archive's docs/ROLLBACK.md: recover paid work, unregister resources while definitions are available, and remove only exact owned keys. Existing equipment may still depend on its MMOItems definitions.

docs.title: Village Trades survival progression
docs.text:
Candidate gameplay guide

These instructions describe unpublished 1.0.0-rc.1 with its exact paired Core build. Public Core compatibility is pending. The server owner must complete setup, including provider templates and mana.

docs.title: First tools and Steel
docs.text:
Craft a Basic Smith's Hammer with two Cobblestone and two Sticks, and Smith's Tongs with two Iron Ingots and one Iron Nugget. Use these crafting-table layouts; a dot means an empty slot:

Tool Rows, top to bottom Basic Smith's Hammer CC. / .S. / .S. Smith's Tongs I.I / .N. / ...

Build an Oven from a stone pressure plate on a smoker. Cook two Raw Iron and one Coal into three Steel, taking 240 loaded ticks (12 seconds at 20 TPS). Charcoal and ordinary Iron Ingots are not substitutes.

Steel is a native MMOItem. Use it to craft equipment blanks at the crafting table. A first Hatchet Blank uses BB. / BS. / ...; a Shortsword Blank uses .B. / .B. / .S.. Here B is Steel and S is a Stick. Browse other exact grids and grade previews through Heirloom's recipe browser.

docs.title: Forge the hatchet
docs.text:
1. Put an anvil on a stripped log and activate it with the Basic Smith's Hammer.
  2. Place the cold blank in the Oven. Use tongs to take it at the desired heat and carry it to an empty smithing anvil.
  3. Hammer, watching the heat gauge. The green temperature band gives better strike quality. Accepted blows use heat; reheat without losing progress as needed.
  4. After 24 accepted blows, heat the shaped piece as needed and quench it with tongs in an unheated water cauldron. This consumes one water level.
  5. Left-click the cauldron to collect the saved finished item.

The one-second hammer cooldown is shared across hammers and workpieces. Hold tongs in the offhand and a hammer in the main hand to move and work without switching. One player can carry one piece, while other pieces rest independently on stations. The workmanship grade combines accepted strike temperature, quench heat and the hammer contributions actually used.

docs.title: Shape a bow or staff
docs.text:
The Woodworking Bench is a Fletching Table. Accept the server pack so its workpiece is visible. Deposit exact ingredients in any order, then left-click the wood with a Village Trades hatchet. The first chop starts the recipe and counts as a stroke.

Product Ingredients before shaping Village Bow 3 Oak Logs + 3 String Bramble Bow 3 Oak Logs + 3 String + Rowan Sprig Carved Staff 2 Oak Logs + Amethyst Shard Doom Staff 2 Oak Logs + Amethyst Shard + Mithral + Soul Sand Rainbow Staff 2 Oak Logs + Amethyst Shard + Mithral + Quartz

Only the logs become the workpiece. Fittings stay beside the wood until finishing. Chop the visible side and let the hatchet's native attack recovery finish between strokes. Broad hits anywhere on the visible wood work; there is no precise-line aiming test. A better hatchet removes more work and improves workmanship. Pausing has no penalty, and one bar tracks the complete shaping process.

Right-click the shaped piece with one Honeycomb to finish it, then left-click to collect. Before waxing, owner sneak-right-click with an empty hand recovers the paid ingredients. After waxing, recovery returns only the saved finished item.

docs.title: Make arrows
docs.text:
On the same bench, deposit one head, one shaft and one fletching. The first hatchet chop starts a four-stroke batch that produces six arrows. An optional Lingering Potion adds its native effects. Each batch has a 50% chance to consume that potion; otherwise the exact potion returns. There is no additional bottle return.

  • Heads: Flint, Iron Ingot, TNT or Glowstone Dust.
  • Shafts: Stick, Bamboo, Bone, Blaze Rod or Breeze Rod.
  • Fletching: Feather, Paper, Phantom Membrane or Amethyst Shard.

Phantom Membrane gives zero gravity. Amethyst fletching locks one visible target near the aimed direction at launch and steers gently, without switching targets or turning through walls. Custom nocked/flying appearances need the accepted pack and PacketEvents; the original native arrow still controls flight and damage.

docs.title: Grow herbs and brew
docs.text:
Discover Normal herbs by breaking Short Grass in Survival. Thyme has a 1% chance in Plains/Meadow; Lemon Balm in Forest/Birch Forest; Comfrey in Swamp/Mangrove Swamp. Natural Oak/Birch Leaves have a 2% chance to drop Rowan Sprig. Persistent player-placed leaves are excluded. Normal protection and acquisition settings apply.

Plant Thyme, Lemon Balm or Comfrey directly on Grass Blocks or Farmland. All six grades can be planted. Base growth is six minutes with 20% variance; harvest one or two herbs and the plant automatically regrows. A harvest has a 10% chance to improve one grade, capped at Perfect. Regrowth retains the planted grade; replant a better herb to improve the plant permanently. Rowan is gathered only.

Start with a Honey Bottle and Thyme in the Boiling Pot for a Small Health Potion. A Glass Bottle, Sugar and Lemon Balm make a Small Mana Potion. Comfrey and Paper in the Mixing Bowl make a poultice. Larger potions and damage tonics build on the same ingredients. Mana restoration requires the server's configured mana pool.

docs.title: Mithral and equipment care
docs.text:
An operator first places a bottom Stone Slab, looks at it within five blocks and runs /hl deposits place VT_MITHRAL_DEPOSIT. /hl deposits inspect shows its state; /hl deposits remove unregisters it and leaves the slab. This candidate has no natural deposit generation.

Mine the registered slab in Survival with an Iron, Diamond or Netherite Pickaxe. Each completed vanilla mining cycle yields one Raw Mithral and uses normal tool durability. Five cycles exhaust the deposit; it replenishes after 15 real minutes, including offline time. Protection denial or unavailable rewards consume nothing. Cook one Raw Mithral and one Netherite Scrap into one Mithral in the Oven, taking 240 loaded ticks. Use Mithral for the Doom and Angel equipment preparations.

Runes use native uncoloured sockets. Tempering Compound upgrades the ordinary Iron Shortsword up to three times; special weapons do not accept it. Unbinding Wax removes and returns one socketed rune. Apply these native consumables to equipment in your inventory rather than using a workstation to socket or upgrade it.

Make a Repair Kit from Steel, Leather and String in the Mixing Bowl, taking 80 ticks. Apply it from the cursor to damaged equipment to restore up to 60 durability. It retains the existing item and its sockets/upgrades. Other packs' custom-durability repair paths can have different cancellation behavior; consult the supplied integration guide before using a kit on valuable equipment from another pack.
