docs.title: Customization
docs.text: Heirloom content is mostly data-driven. Server owners can customize items, recipes, crops, diet labels, seed acquisition, advancements, and visual mappings.

docs.title: Recommended Workflow
docs.text:
1. Make one small JSON change.
  2. Validate the file syntax.
  3. Run /hl reload when the file supports reload.
  4. Search the item or recipe in game.
  5. Craft it once and inspect the output lore.
  6. Only then build the next step of the chain.

This matters because Heirloom recipes can carry metadata forward. A mistake in an intermediate ingredient can affect every later recipe that uses it.

docs.title: Advancements
docs.text: advancements.json controls Heirloom advancement definitions. Advancements can track foods eaten, crops harvested, quality milestones, and recipe progress.

docs.title: Useful Advancement Shapes
docs.text:
• First-time milestones teach players that a system exists.
  • Collections encourage recipe exploration.
  • Quality goals reward farming and mastery.
  • Counters reward repeated cooking or harvesting.

After editing, run /hl reload and test with /hl advancements.

docs.title: CraftEngine Integration
docs.text: CraftEngine is a soft dependency. Use provider-neutral visual_id mappings when a normal Heirloom item only needs a different presentation, or use an exact provider_item reference when a recipe must consume or emit a CraftEngine-owned stack.

docs.title: Exact item references
docs.text:
{ "provider_item": "craftengine:my_pack:tomato" }

The craftengine provider name is case-insensitive, while my_pack:tomato is passed to CraftEngine unchanged. If CraftEngine or the referenced item is unavailable, affected recipes remain visible and unavailable instead of consuming ingredients.

docs.title: Custom Crops
docs.text: Crop JSON defines plant type, growth behavior, planting rules, textures, and harvest drops.

docs.title: Minimum Crop Shape
docs.text: A crop needs an item ID, plant type, growth settings, planting rules, textures, and harvest rules. Use an existing crop close to your desired behavior as the starting point: lettuce for ground crops, tomato for vines, rice for aquatic crops, corn for tall crops.

docs.title: Important Sections
docs.text:
• growth: duration, variance, stages, and scale.
  • planting: valid blocks, item consumption, and permission.
  • textures: growing and ripe display textures.
  • harvest: drops, bonus drops, replanting, sounds, and quality chance.

docs.title: Design Choices
docs.text: Choose a plant type based on physical behavior. A tomato-like crop should be a vine because it needs a wall. A rice-like crop should be aquatic because the water requirement is part of gameplay. Do not use a display offset to fake a crop type that has different block rules.

docs.title: Common Mistakes
docs.text:
• Enabling world generation for a vine crop without natural wall positions.
  • Giving aquatic crops to players before they know the water placement rule.
  • Adding bonus drops that require Fortune, then testing with an unenchanted tool.
  • Forgetting crop permissions when planting works for admins but not players.

docs.title: How To Test
docs.text: Plant it, wait or speed up growth, harvest it, confirm drops, confirm replanting, then test in a protected region with a normal player.

docs.title: Custom Foods
docs.text: Custom foods are defined in JSON under custom_items arrays. A custom food defines the item players can hold; recipes define how players make it.

docs.title: Minimum Edible Food
docs.text:
{
  "id": "GOLDEN_PANCAKE",
  "name": "Golden Pancake",
  "base_material": "PLAYER_HEAD",
  "texture": "http://textures.minecraft.net/texture/...",
  "edible": true,
  "food_value": 8,
  "saturation": 6.0,
  "consume_seconds": 1.4,
  "animation": "EAT",
  "visual_id": "GOLDEN_PANCAKE"
}

docs.title: Advanced Fields To Know
docs.text:
• consume_return: gives an item back after eating.
  • item_model: selects an item model such as minecraft:lingering_potion independently of base_material; a Potion remains drinkable. Juice also uses color for its tint.
  • placeable_servings: makes the food placeable and eaten in servings.
  • feast: enables shared-feast behavior.
  • effects: applies explicit potion effects when eaten.
  • visual_id: lets Nexo, ItemsAdder, CraftEngine, or MMOItems replace the visual without changing recipes.
  • station_texture: uses a cosmetic player-head texture for the ingredient displayed on a station; the original inventory stack remains the source for matching, processing, refunds and recovery.

station_texture belongs to the custom item definition and accepts a real textures.minecraft.net texture URL. It does not change the inventory item or provider mapping. Heirloom Mixology uses it for fruit such as lemons and oranges; omitting it preserves the normal station visual.

docs.title: Common Mistakes
docs.text:
• Defining an item but never adding a recipe for it.
  • Using a pretty name but forgetting the stable uppercase id used in recipes.
  • Expecting a property effect without adding a recipe action or stored property.
  • Using provider-specific visual IDs instead of stable Heirloom visual IDs.

docs.title: How To Test
docs.text: Use /hl give <id> to inspect the item definition, then craft it through the intended recipe to inspect inherited quality, properties, and returns.

docs.title: Custom Recipes
docs.text: Recipes define a station, output, processing time, ingredients, actions, and optional rules. The output can be changed by base actions, rule actions, inherited input metadata, and quality logic.

docs.title: Qualified ingredients
docs.text:
An ingredient may refine a canonical custom identity with an addon-owned qualifier, for example {"custom_item":"DISTILLERY_WINE","qualifier":"distillery:sparkling_wine"}. The addon registers its metadata predicate and cosmetic preview through api.items().registerIngredientQualifier(addonId, qualifierId, canonicalCustomItemId, matches, preview). The owning addon and its item must be active. Matching checks the canonical identity first, then validates the original item's metadata. Missing registrations, missing originals and predicate failures do not match.

Recipes without a qualifier retain their normal meaning: ordinary Wine recipes also accept valid Sparkling Wine. A qualifier cannot be attached to vanilla items, provider items or tags. Rule matchers use options containing the qualified ingredient. Unavailable required qualifiers disable their recipe unless another alternative remains usable. Safe previews preserve appearance and tint without item identity, brewing credentials or effects; they cannot be extracted as genuine ingredients. Registrations participate in reload rollback and addon/item-removal cleanup.

docs.title: Declared Output Variants
docs.text: Decorator-backed dynamic recipes can declare "output_variants": [{"output": "ORCHARD_APPLE_JUICE", "selections": [0]}]. Each entry links a named result to this recipe and supplies one zero-based ingredient-option index per slot for its preview. The decorator still constructs and validates the actual output. Remap selections when optional addon options are filtered. One Juicer recipe supports all pure outputs and mixed juice without duplicate recipes.

docs.title: Minimum Recipe
docs.text:
{
  "id": "SWEET_PANCAKES",
  "station": "FRYING_PAN",
  "output": "PANCAKES",
  "processing_time": 160,
  "ingredients": [
    { "type": "REQUIRED", "max": 1, "options": [{ "custom_item": "BAG_OF_FLOUR" }] },
    { "type": "REQUIRED", "max": 1, "options": [{ "item": "EGG" }] },
    { "type": "OPTIONAL", "max": 1, "options": [{ "item": "HONEY_BOTTLE" }] }
  ],
  "actions": [
    { "type": "SET_PROPERTY", "key": "NAME", "value": "Sweet Pancakes" },
    { "type": "ADD_METADATA", "key": "food_property", "value": "SWEET" }
  ]
}

docs.title: Advanced Pattern: Property Chain
docs.text:
Put properties on intermediate ingredients when you want players to build stronger food through multiple steps. For example, jam can get CHORUS from chorus fruit, then pancakes inherit that property when the jam is used as a topping.

Use required_property on an individual ingredient option when a recipe must accept only a matching ingredient that carries a specific inherited property:

{
  "type": "REQUIRED",
  "max": 1,
  "options": [
    { "custom_item": "DOUGH", "required_property": "CORNMEAL" }
  ]
}

This accepts Dough made from Cornmeal and rejects ordinary flour Dough. Property names are case-insensitive, and the required property appears in recipe previews.

docs.title: Universal recipe item references
docs.text:
Every recipe-emitted item position uses the same identity shape: exactly one of item, custom_item, or provider_item, plus an optional sibling amount. This applies to the primary output, each weighted_outputs entry, every byproducts entry, and the item emitted by SET_RETURN_ITEM or SET_CONSUME_RETURN.

{
  "output": { "custom_item": "PANCAKES", "amount": 2 },
  "weighted_outputs": [
    { "item": "BOWL", "amount": 1, "weight": 5 },
    { "provider_item": "mmoitems:CONSUMABLE:Lucky_Bite", "amount": 1, "weight": 1 }
  ],
  "byproducts": [
    { "item": "GLASS_BOTTLE", "amount": 1 },
    { "provider_item": "craftengine:my_pack:spent_filter", "amount": 1 }
  ],
  "actions": [
    { "type": "SET_RETURN_ITEM", "provider_item": "itemsadder:my_pack:mixing_bowl", "amount": 1 },
    { "type": "SET_CONSUME_RETURN", "provider_item": "mmoitems:MISCELLANEOUS:Empty_Vial", "amount": 1 }
  ]
}

The object form is the preferred authoring format. Existing content remains valid: a legacy string primary output, a weighted entry's legacy output or item, a byproduct's legacy item, and an action's legacy value are all interpreted as item references. Do not put two identity fields in one object; item, custom_item, and provider_item are mutually exclusive. amount belongs next to the chosen identity (and is context-specific: stack size for outputs, byproducts, and returns, never part of the provider ID).

Provider names are normalized (MMOITEMS, mmoitems, and MmoItems name the same provider), but everything after the first colon is provider-owned and preserves its exact casing. For MMOItems, both the TYPE and ID therefore remain exact: mmoitems:SWORD:POISONED_SWORD is not interchangeable with a differently cased suffix.

docs.title: MMOItems sword example
docs.text:
This Cutting Board recipe consumes one MMOItems poison berry, a vanilla iron ingot, and a stick to create an MMOItems sword. The primary output uses the flattened reference directly; the recipe has no separate provider-specific output field.

{
  "id": "MMOITEMS_POISONED_SWORD",
  "station": "CUTTING_BOARD",
  "output": { "provider_item": "mmoitems:SWORD:POISONED_SWORD", "amount": 1 },
  "processing_time": 100,
  "ingredients": [
    { "type": "REQUIRED", "max": 1, "options": [{ "provider_item": "mmoitems:MATERIAL:POISON_BERRIES" }] },
    { "type": "REQUIRED", "max": 1, "options": [{ "item": "IRON_INGOT" }] },
    { "type": "REQUIRED", "max": 1, "options": [{ "item": "STICK" }] }
  ]
}

docs.title: Availability and provider-owned stacks
docs.text:
Providers and their templates are optional. A missing provider or referenced template leaves the recipe registered and visible, but marks it unavailable with the missing reference as the reason. Heirloom preflights the primary result, every weighted alternative, byproducts, and required return references before consuming ingredients; it never partially crafts or consumes inputs after a failed preflight.

Stacks created by a provider are opaque. Heirloom does not add PDC, lore, quality, dietary data, names, textures, visuals, or any other output mutation to them. A provider byproduct cannot set inherit_metadata: true. If any possible primary result is provider-owned, output-mutating actions are invalid, including SET_CONSUME_RETURN; SET_RETURN_ITEM is a separate emitted stack and is not an output mutation. An ordinary Heirloom primary result may use either action to emit a provider craft return or consume return.

docs.title: Common Rule Actions
docs.text:
• SET_PROPERTY with key NAME: changes display name.
  • ADD_METADATA with key food_property: adds a food property that can be inherited and applied when eaten.
  • SET_RETURN_ITEM: emits a return stack when crafting completes; its item reference may be provider-owned.
  • SET_CONSUME_RETURN: records an item reference to emit after eating; it may be provider-owned only when the primary result is an ordinary Heirloom item.
  • SET_VISUAL_ITEM: swaps to a provider-neutral visual variant.
  • ADD_QUALITY and SET_QUALITY: tune output quality.

docs.title: Common Mistakes
docs.text:
• Using SET_PROPERTY for food_property; bundled property recipes use ADD_METADATA for inherited food properties.
  • Putting a custom item in item instead of custom_item.

docs.title: External provider ingredients
docs.text:
Use one provider-prefixed field to accept an exact item owned by Nexo, ItemsAdder, CraftEngine, or MMOItems:

{ "provider_item": "nexo:tomato" }
{ "provider_item": "itemsadder:my_pack:tomato" }
{ "provider_item": "craftengine:my_pack:tomato" }
{ "provider_item": "mmoitems:MATERIAL:POISON_BERRIES" }

Only the first colon is a separator. The provider ID after it is passed unchanged to the provider API. provider_item works in ingredient options and dynamic rule matchers, as well as every recipe-emitted item position described above. Providers remain optional; unavailable options stay visible but cannot match, and other valid options continue to work. Exact provider identity is required, so an external item never matches as its underlying vanilla material. - Forgetting that optional slots default to 0-max, so rules must handle the missing-input case. - Editing JSON and testing only /hl give; recipe actions and inheritance only appear when the recipe is crafted.

docs.title: How To Test
docs.text: Run /hl reload, search the recipe, craft every branch you changed, and inspect lore. For inheritance tests, craft the intermediate ingredient first, then use that exact item in the next recipe.

docs.title: ItemsAdder Integration
docs.text: ItemsAdder is a soft dependency. Heirloom uses the same logical visual_id path for ItemsAdder as it does for Nexo.

docs.title: Recommended Mapping
docs.text: Create ItemsAdder custom stacks for the visual IDs your server wants to replace. Keep IDs stable so recipe actions such as SET_VISUAL_ITEM do not need to change.

docs.title: Fallback Rule
docs.text: If ItemsAdder is missing or an item is not mapped, the normal Heirloom item is still created. Test this fallback before launch so players are not blocked by a visual-pack mistake.

docs.title: MMOItems Integration
docs.text: MMOItems is a soft, optional integration. Heirloom does not bundle MMOItems or MythicLib, and it continues to load when either is absent. Install and configure MMOItems and MythicLib separately before enabling recipes that reference MMOItems stacks.

docs.title: Exact MMOItems references
docs.text:
Use the flattened form mmoitems:<TYPE>:<ID> for inputs and every recipe-emitted item position:

{ "provider_item": "mmoitems:MATERIAL:POISON_BERRIES" }
{ "provider_item": "mmoitems:SWORD:POISONED_SWORD", "amount": 1 }

The provider name is normalized, but the MMOItems suffix is exact and case-preserving. Keep both TYPE and ID exactly as MMOItems defines them. Missing MMOItems or a missing template does not hide or deregister the recipe; Heirloom shows it as unavailable, preflights every weighted result and required emitted reference, and consumes nothing.

docs.title: Resource-pack merge
docs.text:
Normal generated Heirloom visuals use the MMOItems type/id convention MISCELLANEOUS:HEIRLOOM_<ID>. In the supplied YAML fragment, merge each root HEIRLOOM_<ID> entry into plugins/MMOItems/item/miscellaneous.yml; keep its model field inside base. Separately merge mmoitems/resourcepack/assets/heirloom/ into the resource pack your server builds and delivers. MMOItems does not build or distribute that pack for you, and Heirloom does not replace your pack's deployment workflow.

See the official MMOItems item-textures documentation for the resource-pack side of the setup. When MMOItems reloads, Heirloom refreshes the provider on the next Bukkit tick so the refreshed MMOItems registry is ready first.

docs.title: Opaque result rule
docs.text: An MMOItems stack created as a primary result remains owned by MMOItems: Heirloom cannot add lore, PDC, names, textures, quality, dietary data, or a consume return to it. Use an ordinary Heirloom primary output when you need output-mutating actions; that ordinary result may still return an MMOItems stack on craft or consumption.

docs.title: Nexo Integration
docs.text: Nexo is a soft dependency. Heirloom should load without it.

docs.title: Recommended Mapping
docs.text:
Create Nexo items that match Heirloom visual IDs. A common naming convention is:

heirloom_<lowercase_visual_id>

Examples:

heirloom_tomato
heirloom_ice_cream_chorus
heirloom_espresso

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Start the server with Nexo installed, run /hl reload, then create the item through Heirloom rather than directly through Nexo. That proves the provider path is being used by recipes and commands.

docs.title: Seed Acquisition
docs.text:
seed_acquisition.json controls how crops enter survival gameplay.

Use it to configure:

  • Seed packets.
  • Grass drops.
  • Chest loot injection.
  • Natural world patches.

docs.title: Balancing Advice
docs.text:
Use grass drops for common crops, seed packets for curated rewards, chest loot for exploration, and world patches for discovery. Avoid enabling all methods at high rates or rare crops stop feeling rare.

Keep world-generation changes conservative on live servers. They only affect new chunks and can make rare crops too common if patch chances are high.

docs.title: Visual Integrations Overview
docs.text: Heirloom works without a resource pack by using vanilla materials and player-head textures. Optional providers can replace that presentation.

docs.title: Provider-Neutral Flow
docs.text:
1. Item definitions declare visual_id.
  2. Recipes can call SET_VISUAL_ITEM.
  3. VisualItemResolver asks registered providers for that visual.
  4. If no provider has it, Heirloom falls back to the normal item.

This keeps visual mapping data independent from Nexo, ItemsAdder, CraftEngine, or MMOItems. Direct provider_item recipe references are a different feature: use them only when the recipe deliberately requires or emits that provider's exact stack.

docs.title: Practical Rule
docs.text: Use Heirloom item IDs and visual IDs as stable public names. Let Nexo, ItemsAdder, CraftEngine, or MMOItems map those names to models. Do not bake a provider namespace into a recipe unless the recipe deliberately needs that exact provider stack.

docs.title: Web Generator Workflow
docs.text:
The web generator is useful when you do not want to hand-write recipe JSON.

Use it to draft recipes, then review the exported JSON before putting it on a production server.

Recommended workflow:

  1. Build the recipe in the generator.
  2. Export JSON.
  3. Paste into the correct recipe file.
  4. Validate JSON formatting.
  5. Run /hl reload.
  6. Test with /hl search <recipe>.
  7. Craft the recipe once to confirm actions, inherited properties, return items, and visuals.

Generator link: https://kernel-person.github.io/heirloom-generator/

docs.title: Developer API
docs.text: Integrate external Paper plugins with Heirloom 2.11.0 to inspect FoodFactsV2 dietary provenance, create or identify custom foods, listen to cooking/harvest/consumption events, and register programmatic items, recipes, crops, aging stages, advancements, or cookbook guides.

docs.title: Maven Repository & Dependency
docs.text:
Add the public Heirloom Maven repository and compile against ke.ric:heirloom-api:2.11.0 (Java 21+, Paper 1.21.11+).

  • Repository URL: https://heirloom-maven.pages.dev
  • Coordinates: ke.ric:heirloom-api:2.11.0
  • Online Javadocs: https://heirloom-maven.pages.dev/javadoc/
Gradle (Kotlin DSL)Gradle (Groovy)Maven (pom.xml)plugin.yml 
repositories {
    mavenCentral()
    maven("https://repo.papermc.io/repository/maven-public/")
    maven("https://heirloom-maven.pages.dev")
}

dependencies {
    compileOnly("io.papermc.paper:paper-api:1.21.11-R0.1-SNAPSHOT")
    compileOnly("ke.ric:heirloom-api:2.11.0")
}

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
    maven { url 'https://repo.papermc.io/repository/maven-public/' }
    maven { url 'https://heirloom-maven.pages.dev' }
}

dependencies {
    compileOnly 'io.papermc.paper:paper-api:1.21.11-R0.1-SNAPSHOT'
    compileOnly 'ke.ric:heirloom-api:2.11.0'
}

<repositories>
    <repository>
        <id>papermc</id>
        <url>https://repo.papermc.io/repository/maven-public/</url>
    </repository>
    <repository>
        <id>heirloom-maven</id>
        <url>https://heirloom-maven.pages.dev</url>
    </repository>
</repositories>

<dependencies>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>io.papermc.paper</groupId>
        <artifactId>paper-api</artifactId>
        <version>1.21.11-R0.1-SNAPSHOT</version>
        <scope>provided</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>ke.ric</groupId>
        <artifactId>heirloom-api</artifactId>
        <version>2.11.0</version>
        <scope>provided</scope>
    </dependency>
</dependencies>

# Hard dependency if Heirloom is required:
depend: [Heirloom]

# Or soft dependency when integrating optionally:
softdepend: [Heirloom]

Compile-Only SDK — Never Shade

ke.ric:heirloom-api ships compile-only API stubs whose methods throw UnsupportedOperationException if bundled into your plugin JAR. Always keep it compileOnly (Gradle) or <scope>provided</scope> (Maven) so Paper loads the real implementation from the Heirloom plugin at runtime.

IDE Autocomplete, Parameter Names & Hover Javadocs

heirloom-maven.pages.dev publishes heirloom-api-2.11.0-javadoc.jar and heirloom-api-2.11.0-sources.jar alongside .jar, and compiles bytecode with -parameters. IntelliJ IDEA, VS Code, and Eclipse automatically show full parameter names, Javadoc descriptions, and usage snippets on hover after syncing Gradle or Maven.

docs.title: Accessing HeirloomAPI
docs.text:
Verify that Heirloom is enabled before calling API methods, then check api.isReady() before performing registrations or runtime lookups:

import ke.ric.api.HeirloomAPI;
import org.bukkit.Bukkit;
import org.bukkit.plugin.Plugin;
import org.bukkit.plugin.java.JavaPlugin;

public final class MyIntegrationPlugin extends JavaPlugin {
    @Override
    public void onEnable() {
        Plugin heirloomPlugin = Bukkit.getPluginManager().getPlugin("Heirloom");
        if (heirloomPlugin == null || !heirloomPlugin.isEnabled()) {
            return;
        }

        HeirloomAPI api = HeirloomAPI.getInstance();
        if (api == null || !api.isReady()) {
            return;
        }

        // Safe to read items, listen to events, or register addons
    }
}

docs.title: Addons & Content Registration
docs.text: Heirloom manages addon lifetimes, owner-scoped registrations, and safe rollback transactions across /hl reload through HeirloomAPI and the ke.ric.api.registration facades.

docs.title: Registering & Reloading an Addon
docs.text:
Prefer the callback registerAddon overloads on HeirloomAPI so your plugin does not depend on cross-classloader interface timing. Pass an enable callback, plus optional reload and cleanup callbacks:

import ke.ric.api.HeirloomAPI;
import org.bukkit.Bukkit;
import org.bukkit.plugin.Plugin;
import org.bukkit.plugin.java.JavaPlugin;

public final class MyFoodAddon extends JavaPlugin {
    private static final String ADDON_ID = "my_food_addon";

    @Override
    public void onEnable() {
        Plugin heirloom = Bukkit.getPluginManager().getPlugin("Heirloom");
        if (heirloom == null || !heirloom.isEnabled()) {
            return;
        }
        HeirloomAPI api = HeirloomAPI.getInstance();
        if (api == null || !api.isReady()) {
            return;
        }

        api.registerAddon(
                ADDON_ID,
                getPluginMeta().getVersion(),
                this,
                this::registerContent,
                this::onHeirloomReload,
                this::onHeirloomDisable
        );
    }

    private void registerContent(HeirloomAPI api) {
        // Items, crops, recipes, aging, advancements, and guides registered here
        // are automatically tracked under ADDON_ID
    }

    private void onHeirloomReload() {
        reloadConfig();
    }

    private void onHeirloomDisable() {
        // Released when Heirloom unregisters this addon independently
    }
}

Available registration and lifecycle methods on HeirloomAPI:

  • registerAddon(String addonId, String version, Plugin owningPlugin, Consumer<HeirloomAPI> registrationCallback)
  • registerAddon(..., Runnable reloadCallback) / registerAddon(..., Runnable reloadCallback, Runnable disableCallback)
  • registerAddon(Plugin owningPlugin, HeirloomAddon addon) — legacy interface variant (getAddonId(), getVersion(), onEnable(HeirloomAPI), onReload(), onDisable())
  • unregisterAddon(String addonId) — removes the addon and all owner-scoped registrations
  • isAddonRegistered(String addonId) / getAddon(String addonId)
  • registerReloadState(String addonId, Supplier<Runnable> snapshot) — participates in /hl reload rollback if a reload fails partway through
  • withAddonRegistrationContext(String addonId, Runnable registration) — executes deferred updates under an explicit addon owner context

docs.title: Registration Facades
docs.text:
Access each owner-scoped registry directly from HeirloomAPI:

Facade Method Accepts in register(...) Items api.items() ItemRegistration.ItemDefinitionBuilder Recipes api.recipes() RecipeRegistration.AddonRecipeBuilder Crops api.crops() CropRegistration.CropDefinitionBuilder Seed Acquisition api.seedAcquisition() File (registerFromFile(File, String addonId)) Dietary Properties api.properties() PropertyRegistration.PropertyDefinitionBuilder Advancements api.advancements() AdvancementDefinition record Cellar / Rack Aging api.aging() AgingDefinition (AgingDefinition.builder()...build()) Addon Cookbook Guides api.guides() GuideDefinition record

Do not call .build() inside items(), recipes(), crops(), or properties().register(...)

api.items().register(...), api.recipes().register(...), api.crops().register(...), and api.properties().register(...) take the builder directly, not .build(). By contrast, api.aging().register(...), api.advancements().register(...), and api.guides().register(...) take constructed records (AgingDefinition.builder()...build(), new AdvancementDefinition(...), new GuideDefinition(...)).

docs.title: Custom Items (api.items())
docs.text:
Register items programmatically with ItemRegistration.builder() or load editable JSON definitions via registerFromFile(File, defaultAddonId). You can also register custom ingredient recognizers or qualifiers so specialized items match Heirloom recipe inputs cleanly:

import ke.ric.api.registration.ItemRegistration;
import org.bukkit.potion.PotionEffectType;

api.items().register(ItemRegistration.builder()
        .id("HONEY_GLAZED_APPLE")
        .name("Honey Glazed Apple")
        .texture("http://textures.minecraft.net/texture/...")
        .edible(true)
        .foodValue(6)
        .saturation(0.7f)
        .consumeSeconds(1.6f)
        .animation("EAT")
        .canAlwaysEat(false)
        .tags("SWEET", "FRUIT")
        .addEffect(PotionEffectType.REGENERATION, 100, 0, 1.0f));

Useful helpers on ItemRegistration: isRegistered(id), registeredIds(addonId), registerIngredientRecognizer(addonId, customItemId, predicate), registerIngredientQualifier(addonId, qualifierId, canonicalCustomItemId, matches, preview), unregisterProgrammaticAddon(addonId).

docs.title: Custom Recipes (api.recipes())
docs.text:
Create addon recipes under your addon category, register editable JSON catalogs (registerFromFile), suppress existing recipes with override strength (suppress(addonId, recipeId, overrideStrength)), or hook runtime output creation/decoration/eligibility:

import ke.ric.api.registration.RecipeRegistration;
import ke.ric.cooking.data.RecipeItemRef;

api.recipes().register(RecipeRegistration.builder()
        .id("MYADDON_BREW_MEAD")
        .addonId("my_food_addon")
        .stationName("Fermenting Vat")
        .output(RecipeItemRef.customItem("GOLDEN_MEAD"), 1)
        .processingTimeSeconds(30)
        .addIngredient("HONEY_BOTTLE", false, 2)
        .addIngredient("WHEAT", false, 1));

Additional hooks on RecipeRegistration: - registerOutputHandler(recipeId, CustomOutputHandler) — produce dynamic outputs from actual inputs - registerOutputDecorator(addonId, recipeId, RecipeOutputDecorator) — annotate or adjust crafted stacks in place - registerEligibilityPredicate(recipeId, RecipeEligibilityPredicate) — enforce custom pre-craft checks before inputs are reserved - inspectFile(File, defaultAddonId, customItemExists) — validate editable recipe files offline without mutating registries - Helper factories: RecipeRegistration.vanillaItemMatcher(materialId), customItemMatcher(customItemId), action(type, key, value), visualAction(visualId), nameAction(displayName)

docs.title: Crops & Seed Acquisition (api.crops(), api.seedAcquisition())
docs.text:
import ke.ric.api.registration.CropRegistration;
import org.bukkit.Material;
import org.bukkit.Sound;

api.crops().register(CropRegistration.builder()
        .id("BLUEBERRY_BUSH")
        .itemId("BLUEBERRY")
        .plantType("SHORT_PLANT")
        .growthDuration(600)
        .growthStages(4)
        .validPlantingBlocks(Material.FARMLAND, Material.GRASS_BLOCK)
        .harvestDrop("BLUEBERRY", 2, 4)
        .replantAfterHarvest(true)
        .sounds(Sound.BLOCK_SWEET_BERRY_BUSH_PICK_BERRIES, Sound.BLOCK_CROP_BREAK)
        .textures("http://textures.minecraft.net/texture/...", "http://textures.minecraft.net/texture/..."));

Register custom plant growth behaviors via api.crops().registerPlantType(PlantType, addonId) and load addon seed packets, biome grass drops, chest loot, and block drops via SeedAcquisitionRegistration (api.seedAcquisition().registerFromFile(file, addonId)).

docs.title: Dietary Properties (api.properties())
docs.text:
import ke.ric.api.registration.PropertyRegistration;

api.properties().register(PropertyRegistration.builder()
        .id("CAFFEINE_FREE")
        .displayName("Caffeine-Free")
        .displayIcon("🍵")
        .description("Contains no coffee or tea")
        .violatorCustomItems("ESPRESSO", "MATCHA_LATTE"));

docs.title: Advancements (api.advancements())
docs.text:
import ke.ric.api.advancement.AdvancementDefinition;

api.advancements().register(AdvancementDefinition.hiddenChallenge(
        "taste_golden_mead",
        "Cellar Connoisseur",
        "Sample a bottle of Golden Mead",
        "GOLDEN_MEAD",
        null
));

docs.title: Cellar / Rack Aging (api.aging())
docs.text:
Define owner-scoped timed aging stages (with AgingConditions, AgingEnvironmentProbes, dynamic outcomes, and in-place item preservation):

import ke.ric.api.aging.AgingCondition;
import ke.ric.api.aging.AgingDefinition;
import ke.ric.api.aging.AgingStage;
import java.time.Duration;

api.aging().register(AgingDefinition.builder()
        .id("myaddon:aged_mead")
        .input("YOUNG_MEAD")
        .stage(AgingStage.of("Rested", Duration.ofMinutes(10), AgingCondition.ZERO_SKYLIGHT, AgingCondition.COOL))
        .output("GOLDEN_MEAD")
        .outputYield(1)
        .build());

docs.title: Cookbook Guides (api.guides())
docs.text:
Register custom addon hub entries, routed guide pages, exact ingredient production deep links (registerProductionDestination), tag destinations (registerTagProductionDestination), and custom non-recipe item uses (registerItemUse):

import ke.ric.api.guide.GuideDefinition;
import ke.ric.api.guide.GuideDestination;
import ke.ric.api.guide.GuidePage;
import ke.ric.cooking.data.RecipeItemRef;
import java.util.List;

api.guides().register(new GuideDefinition(
        "myaddon_guide",
        10,
        player -> api.createItem("GOLDEN_MEAD"),
        player -> new GuidePage("My Food Addon", List.of())
));

api.guides().registerProductionDestination(
        RecipeItemRef.customItem("GOLDEN_MEAD"),
        null,
        new GuideDestination("myaddon_guide", "mead_overview")
);

docs.title: Bukkit Events
docs.text: Heirloom fires five Bukkit events under ke.ric.api.events so addons and external plugins can react to food consumption, placed feasts, station crafting, crop harvesting, and /hl give grants.

docs.title: Event Summary
docs.text: Event Class Cancellable Primary Data HeirloomFoodConsumedEvent Yes getPlayer(), getItem(), getCustomItemId(), isCustomItem(), get/setHungerRestored(), get/setSaturationRestored() HeirloomPlacedFoodConsumedEvent No (final) getPlayer(), getItem(), getCustomItemId() HeirloomItemCraftedEvent Yes getPlayer(), getStation(), getRecipeId(), get/setResult() HeirloomCropHarvestedEvent Yes getPlayer(), getLocation(), getCropDefinition(), getCropId(), get/setDrops(), addDrop(), willReplant(), setWillReplant() HeirloomAdminItemEvent Yes (final) getPlayer(), getItemId(), getItem()

docs.title: HeirloomFoodConsumedEvent
docs.text: Fired after vanilla PlayerItemConsumeEvent when a player eats or drinks a Heirloom food item (or vanilla food handled by Heirloom). Modify hunger/saturation restoration or cancel consumption before Heirloom applies effects.

docs.title: HeirloomPlacedFoodConsumedEvent
docs.text:
Fired after a player eats one serving from a placed world food or feast (non-cancellable). The attached getItem() stack preserves the placed block's original FoodFactsV2 metadata, making this the right hook for dietary/beliefs tracking on placed servings alongside HeirloomFoodConsumedEvent / PlayerItemConsumeEvent.

import ke.ric.api.HeirloomAPI;
import ke.ric.api.events.HeirloomFoodConsumedEvent;
import ke.ric.api.events.HeirloomPlacedFoodConsumedEvent;
import ke.ric.api.food.FoodFactsV2;
import org.bukkit.event.EventHandler;
import org.bukkit.event.Listener;
import org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack;

public final class ConsumptionListener implements Listener {
    @EventHandler(ignoreCancelled = true)
    public void onFoodConsumed(HeirloomFoodConsumedEvent event) {
        if (event.isCustomItem() && "HONEY_CAKE".equals(event.getCustomItemId())) {
            event.setHungerRestored(event.getHungerRestored() + 2);
            event.setSaturationRestored(event.getSaturationRestored() + 1.5f);
        }
    }

    @EventHandler
    public void onPlacedServingConsumed(HeirloomPlacedFoodConsumedEvent event) {
        ItemStack serving = event.getItem();
        FoodFactsV2 facts = HeirloomAPI.getInstance().foodFactsV2(serving);
        // Inspect facts.categories() / facts.dietaryFacts() for this serving
    }
}

docs.title: HeirloomItemCraftedEvent
docs.text:
Fired when a player crafts a recipe at one of Heirloom's cooking stations (ke.ric.cooking.CookingStation):

OVEN, BOILING_POT, MIXING_BOWL, CUTTING_BOARD, FRYING_PAN, BARISTA_MACHINE, MIXOLOGY_TABLE, JUICER, FARMHOUSE_PRESS

Cancelling prevents the result from being awarded; setResult(ItemStack) swaps the output item (Core updates FoodFactsV2 lineage after approved result replacements).

import ke.ric.api.events.HeirloomItemCraftedEvent;
import ke.ric.cooking.CookingStation;
import org.bukkit.event.EventHandler;
import org.bukkit.event.Listener;

public final class CraftListener implements Listener {
    @EventHandler(ignoreCancelled = true)
    public void onCraft(HeirloomItemCraftedEvent event) {
        if (event.getStation() == CookingStation.OVEN && "APPLE_PIE".equals(event.getRecipeId())) {
            // Adjust or log crafted result
        }
    }
}

docs.title: HeirloomCropHarvestedEvent
docs.text:
Fired when a player harvests a mature Heirloom custom crop. Add bonus drops with addDrop(ItemStack), replace drops via setDrops(List<ItemStack>), toggle auto-replanting via setWillReplant(boolean), or cancel the harvest.

import ke.ric.api.events.HeirloomCropHarvestedEvent;
import org.bukkit.Material;
import org.bukkit.event.EventHandler;
import org.bukkit.event.Listener;
import org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack;

public final class HarvestListener implements Listener {
    @EventHandler(ignoreCancelled = true)
    public void onCropHarvested(HeirloomCropHarvestedEvent event) {
        if ("TOMATO".equals(event.getCropId())) {
            event.addDrop(new ItemStack(Material.STICK, 1));
            event.setWillReplant(true);
        }
    }
}

docs.title: HeirloomAdminItemEvent
docs.text: Fired before delivering a fresh stack granted through /hl give or the admin cheat GUI (never fired for recipe browser previews, existing inventories, or normal crafting). Addons that initialize playable item metadata on spawned samples should listen here and avoid cancelling legitimate grants unless policy forbids the item.

docs.title: Items & FoodFacts V2
docs.text: Heirloom provides item factory/identification helpers on HeirloomAPI, immutable FoodFactsV2 evidence for ingredient lineage and dietary truth, and shared beverage/alcohol metadata helpers under ke.ric.api.item.

docs.title: Custom Item Lookups & Creation
docs.text:
All item helpers live on HeirloomAPI:

Method Return Behaviour api.createItem(String itemId) ItemStack Creates one custom item stack, or returns null if itemId is unknown. api.createItem(String itemId, int amount) ItemStack Creates a custom item stack with the given amount, or returns null if unknown. api.isCustomItem(ItemStack item) boolean Returns true if the stack carries a registered Heirloom custom item identity. api.getCustomItemId(ItemStack item) String Returns the custom item ID (e.g. "TOMATO_SOUP"), or null for non-Heirloom items. 
HeirloomAPI api = HeirloomAPI.getInstance();
if (api != null && api.isReady()) {
    ItemStack soup = api.createItem("TOMATO_SOUP");
    if (api.isCustomItem(heldItem)) {
        String customId = api.getCustomItemId(heldItem);
        getLogger().info("Player holds Heirloom item: " + customId);
    }
}

docs.title: Reading Dietary Evidence (FoodFactsV2)
docs.text:
Prefer api.foodFactsV2(item) (or FoodFactsV2.read(item)) for dietary checks. It inspects an ItemStack read-only and never reconstructs missing recipe history or mutates the item.

import ke.ric.api.HeirloomAPI;
import ke.ric.api.food.FoodFactsV2;

FoodFactsV2 facts = HeirloomAPI.getInstance().foodFactsV2(itemStack);

// Access dietary truth conservatively via the map (absent keys mean UNKNOWN)
FoodFactsV2.Truth vegan = facts.dietaryFacts()
        .getOrDefault("VEGAN", FoodFactsV2.Truth.UNKNOWN);

if (vegan == FoodFactsV2.Truth.FALSE || facts.categories().contains("PORK")) {
    // Confirmed non-vegan or contains pork
} else if (vegan == FoodFactsV2.Truth.TRUE && facts.categoriesComplete()) {
    // Confirmed vegan with complete category classification
}

docs.title: FoodFactsV2 Record Components
docs.text:
ke.ric.api.food.FoodFactsV2 is an immutable Java record with seven accessors:

Accessor Type Meaning itemId() String Source-qualified logical identity (heirloom:<id>, minecraft:<material>, or <provider>:<item>), or null for empty/air items. ingredientIds() Set<String> Immutable sorted set of observed source-qualified ingredient IDs (flattened across crafted steps). categories() Set<String> Immutable sorted set of uppercase dietary categories (see standard categories below). tags() Set<String> Immutable sorted set of normalized uppercase custom tags. dietaryFacts() Map<String, FoodFactsV2.Truth> Map of dietary flag keys to TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN. An absent key also means UNKNOWN. complete() boolean true when every contributing ingredient lineage is known. categoriesComplete() boolean true when every known ingredient's category classification is complete (independent of complete()).

docs.title: Tri-State Truth (TRUE / FALSE / UNKNOWN)
docs.text:
Heirloom uses three-valued logic (FoodFactsV2.Truth) so custom or unknown items never falsely claim to be safe:

  • Truth.TRUE — Established from complete supported source evidence or an explicit producer certification with no contradicting adverse evidence.
  • Truth.FALSE — An ingredient or classification explicitly violates the property (adverse evidence survives unknown ingredients).
  • Truth.UNKNOWN — Evidence is incomplete or absent (for example an opaque third-party item or legacy stack without V2 lineage). Treat missing keys in dietaryFacts() identically to Truth.UNKNOWN.

docs.title: Built-In Dietary Flags & Standard Categories
docs.text:
Check these uppercase keys in facts.dietaryFacts() and uppercase elements in facts.categories():

  • Built-in dietaryFacts() keys: PORK_FREE, BEEF_FREE, MEAT_FREE, VEGETARIAN, VEGAN, PESCATARIAN, ALCOHOL_FREE, GLUTEN_FREE
  • Standard categories() values: PLANT, ANIMAL, PORK, BEEF, MEAT, FISH, DAIRY, EGG, HONEY, GLUTEN, ALCOHOL, MINERAL, WATER

Legacy V1 API

api.foodFacts(ItemStack) returns the legacy V1 ke.ric.api.food.FoodFacts record (itemId, ingredientIds, categories, tags, dietaryFacts, complete). Keep V1 only for backwards compatibility; use FoodFactsV2 for new integrations.

docs.title: Propagating Lineage on Custom Station Outputs
docs.text:
If your plugin crafts or transforms food stacks using actual consumed input items, record the production boundary right where the real input ItemStacks are still available:

// Read inputs before mutating output (supports in-place stack updates)
FoodFactsV2.writeProduced(outputStack, actualConsumedInputs, "myaddon:spiced_stew");
  • The third argument is a source-qualified fallback output ID used only when outputStack has no actual custom owner.
  • Include unknown/null input entries instead of omitting them so complete() stays honest.
  • When merging snapshots in memory without direct stack mutation, call FoodFactsV2.produced(resultFacts, inputFacts) and apply the returned record via FoodFactsV2.write(outputStack, merged).
  • For identity-preserving refreshes (updating lore/visuals without consuming new ingredients), copy evidence directly instead of calling FoodFactsV2.produced(...):
FoodFactsV2.write(refreshedItem, FoodFactsV2.read(originalItem));

docs.title: Zero-Dependency PDC JSON Schema (heirloom:food_facts_v2)
docs.text:
External plugins that do not depend on heirloom-api at compile time (or support older Heirloom jars) can read the PersistentDataContainer key heirloom:food_facts_v2 as PersistentDataType.STRING:

{
  "version": 2,
  "itemId": "heirloom:vegetable_pie",
  "ingredientIds": ["heirloom:dough", "minecraft:carrot", "minecraft:wheat"],
  "categories": ["GLUTEN", "PLANT"],
  "tags": [],
  "dietaryFacts": {
    "GLUTEN_FREE": "FALSE",
    "VEGAN": "TRUE"
  },
  "complete": true,
  "categoriesComplete": true
}
  • Only consume a payload whose integer "version" equals 2.
  • Always check actual alcohol evidence if present: positive actual ABV metadata always implies ALCOHOL and ALCOHOL_FREE = FALSE.

docs.title: Beverage, Quality & Tooltip Utilities (ke.ric.api.item)
docs.text:
The ke.ric.api.item package exposes shared helpers for drinks and generated lore without depending on Distillery internals:

Class Key Methods Purpose DrinkQuality level(ItemStack) / level(ItemStack, int fallback) Read Heirloom item quality consistently across food and drink items. TerminalAlcohol read(ItemStack) / isMarked(ItemStack) / write(ItemStack) Read or stamp terminal mixed-drink ABV, quality, and integration state (record TerminalAlcohol(double abv, int quality, boolean integrated)). DrinkServing read(ItemStack) / write(ItemStack, double) / equivalentCl(double abv, double volumeCl) / DEFAULT_CL (4.0) / REFERENCE_ABV (40.0) Standardize drink serving volume and inebriation scaling. AlcoholLore estimate(abv, servingCl) / range(minAbv, maxAbv, servingCl) / apply(...) / refresh(ItemStack) Render standardized alcohol lore and catalog preview lines. PotionTooltip hideEmptyEffectTooltip(ItemStack) / hideEffectTooltip(ItemStack) Hide vanilla empty "No Effects" rows on custom potion-based items.

docs.title: Food Systems
docs.text: Heirloom food is more than hunger points. Items can carry quality, dietary labels, food properties, potion effects, creator data, consume returns, and visual IDs.

docs.title: The Important Distinction
docs.text:
• Dietary properties answer "what is this food made from?" Examples: vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free.
  • Food properties answer "what happens when I eat this?" Examples: golden, chorus, sweet, energizing.
  • Quality answers "how well did this food turn out?"

These systems can overlap on one item. A high-quality vegan food can also be GOLDEN, CHORUS, and a player's favourite food.

docs.title: Dietary Properties
docs.text:
Dietary labels use a blacklist model. A recipe is assumed to satisfy a property unless one of its ingredients violates that property.

Property Display Meaning Implies VEGAN Vegan Contains no animal products VEGETARIAN VEGETARIAN Vegetarian Contains no meat or fish GLUTEN_FREE Gluten-Free Contains no gluten

docs.title: How Calculation Works
docs.text: When a recipe is previewed or crafted, Heirloom checks the selected ingredients. Vanilla ingredients are compared against dietary config. Custom ingredients can already carry stored dietary data, so a later recipe does not need to know every raw ingredient that originally created them.

docs.title: Inheritance Example
docs.text: If a custom sauce was made with milk, and that sauce is later used in a sandwich, the sandwich should not become vegan just because the sandwich recipe only sees SAUCE. Stored dietary data keeps that history attached to the ingredient.

docs.title: Example: Adding Kosher Or Halal
docs.text:
You can add server-specific dietary rules the same way the bundled file defines VEGAN, VEGETARIAN, and GLUTEN_FREE. The important idea is that a property describes what is allowed, and its violators list describes what breaks that rule.

For example, a simple halal-style rule might blacklist pork materials and pork-based custom foods:

"HALAL": {
  "display_name": "Halal",
  "description": "Contains no server-defined non-halal ingredients",
  "violators": {
    "items": [
      "PORKCHOP",
      "COOKED_PORKCHOP"
    ],
    "custom_items": [
      "BACON",
      "CHRISTMAS_HAM"
    ]
  }
}

A simple kosher-style rule can use the same structure:

"KOSHER": {
  "display_name": "Kosher",
  "description": "Contains no server-defined non-kosher ingredients",
  "violators": {
    "items": [
      "PORKCHOP",
      "COOKED_PORKCHOP"
    ],
    "custom_items": [
      "BACON",
      "CHRISTMAS_HAM"
    ]
  }
}

After adding those entries under dietary_properties, reload and test a few chains. If BACON is made from PORKCHOP, the bacon will not receive HALAL or KOSHER. If that bacon is later used in EGGS_AND_BACON, BLT, or a custom burger, the finished food also will not receive those properties because custom ingredients carry their stored dietary data forward.

Note

Heirloom enforces the rules you configure; it does not decide real-world religious law. If your server also wants to treat alcohol, shellfish, meat-and-dairy combinations, or specific addon drinks as disallowed, add those vanilla or custom item IDs to the appropriate violators lists and test the recipe chains players actually use.

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text: hierarchy_rules hide weaker labels when a stronger label is present. Bundled data treats VEGAN as implying VEGETARIAN, so vegan foods do not need to show both labels.

docs.title: Contains Lines
docs.text: The contains_settings block controls "Contains:" lore. Use it for practical warnings, not just marketing labels. It is most useful for common allergens, roleplay restrictions, or server-specific diet rules.

docs.title: Favourite And Social Bonuses
docs.text: Favourite food and cooked-by metadata are player-data systems. They are separate from recipe matching, but they can combine with food properties at eating time.

docs.title: Favourite Food
docs.text:
Players choose a favourite with /hl favourite. Eating that custom food grants:

Effect Duration Strength Regeneration 30 seconds I Saturation 15 seconds II Luck 60 seconds I

The favourite check runs after food-property effects. A property-stacked favourite therefore applies both sets of behavior.

docs.title: Cooked By
docs.text: When a player crafts edible output, Heirloom can store the crafter UUID. Later, favourite-food checks can reward the cook with a short regeneration effect if somebody else eats the favourite food they made.

docs.title: Affinity
docs.text: AFFINITY also reads cooked-by metadata. If the food was cooked by someone else, it grants regeneration to the eater. If that same food is also the eater's favourite, the regeneration amplifier is increased.

docs.title: Data Storage
docs.text: Player RPG data is saved under plugins/Heirloom/playerdata/. Favourite choice and mastery are stored per player.

docs.title: Food Properties
docs.text: Food properties are gameplay tags stored on the item. They are not just wiki categories: when you eat the item, Heirloom loops over every stored property and applies the matching behavior.

docs.title: Where Properties Come From
docs.text:
A property can be added by a recipe action, usually ADD_METADATA with key food_property, or it can already exist on an ingredient. When a recipe finishes, Heirloom starts with properties already on the output, then adds every property found on every input item. The result is stored back on the output and shown in lore.

That means properties can stack through recipe chains.

docs.title: Worked Example: Powerful Pancakes
docs.text:
1. Make jam in the Boiling Pot with CHORUS_FRUIT. The jam rule adds CHORUS.
  2. Make another jam with GOLDEN_APPLE. The jam rule adds GOLDEN.
  3. Use property-bearing jam as a pancake topping in the Frying Pan. Pancakes inherit the jam's stored properties.
  4. Eat the pancakes. The food applies every stored food property, then any JSON-defined effects, then favourite-food effects if pancakes are your favourite.

In bundled data, honey pancakes add honey naming, quality, and bottle return behavior. Honey does not add SWEET to pancakes unless a recipe or custom item explicitly stores SWEET as a food property. Server owners can add that behavior with recipe actions.

docs.title: Exact Property Effects
docs.text: Property Effect when eaten GLOWING Glowing I for 30 seconds, beacon-style sound/message GOLDEN Regeneration II for 5 seconds and Absorption I for 2 minutes CHORUS Attempts a safe random teleport, like chorus fruit SWEET Speed I and Haste I for 10 seconds SPICY Fire Resistance I for 20 seconds, plus 1 second of visual fire COLD Slowness I for 5 seconds and Resistance II for 10 seconds ENERGIZING Speed II, Haste II, and Jump Boost I for 30 seconds NOURISHING Saturation III for 5 seconds HEALING Instant Health II AFFINITY If cooked by another player, Regeneration I for 10 seconds; Regeneration II if it is also your favourite food SOBERING If Distillery is loaded and inebriation is enabled, drains drunkenness by the configured amount, default 0.6‰, once per consumed serving

docs.title: What Players See
docs.text: The recipe browser preview can show food-property lore based on the selected ingredients. Finished items also carry the property lore. If the final food is placed as a serving food, the placed block stores the properties too, so bites can still apply the behavior.

docs.title: Server Owner Pattern
docs.text:
Use properties for intentional power chains. For example, a server could make maple syrup add SWEET, then pancakes made with GOLDEN jam and syrup would carry both the inherited jam property and the syrup property.

{
  "type": "ADD_METADATA",
  "key": "food_property",
  "value": "SWEET"
}

Avoid relying on hidden balance. If a food should heal, sober, teleport, energize, or become a strong favourite-food candidate, put that behavior in the recipe or ingredient data.

docs.title: Quality And Effects
docs.text: Quality is stored on custom foods and ingredients. Crops can preserve and improve quality, recipes can set or add quality, and mastery can improve final results.

docs.title: Quality Sources
docs.text:
• SET_QUALITY gives an output a specific value.
  • ADD_QUALITY increases the current value when a rule matches.
  • If no explicit quality is supplied, crafted custom foods can inherit the best numeric quality from their inputs.
  • Cooking Mastery adds a recipe-specific quality bonus to future crafts.
  • Crops can store quality and keep it when replanted.

docs.title: Effect Sources
docs.text:
An eaten item can apply effects from:

  • Its normal food value and saturation.
  • Its food_property tags.
  • Its JSON effects list.
  • Favourite food behavior.
  • Cooked-by social behavior.
  • Distillery sobering integration if SOBERING is present.

docs.title: Debugging Balance
docs.text:
If a food is too weak, check whether the recipe actually adds a property or effect. If it is too strong, check inherited ingredients first; an intermediate item may be carrying properties into many later recipes.

Prepared foods should follow configured values. If a food needs regeneration, saturation, or another potion effect, define it explicitly in JSON.

docs.title: Gardening
docs.text:
Heirloom crops use custom display visuals and growth stages.

Core crops are Lettuce, Onion, Corn, Tomato, and Rice. Addons can register additional crops, such as Distillery grapes and Cafe coffee cherries.

docs.title: Crop Gallery
docs.text: Lettuce: Short ground crop. Onion: Allium-style ground crop. Corn: Tall crop with vertical room. Tomato: Wall vine crop. Rice: Aquatic crop planted in water.

docs.title: What A Crop Is
docs.text: A crop is a real block plus a display entity and stored data. The block gives Minecraft something to protect, break, and interact with; the display gives Heirloom its custom visual stages; stored data tracks crop ID, growth state, facing, and optional quality.

docs.title: The Growth Loop
docs.text:
1. Obtain a crop item or seed packet.
  2. Plant it on a valid block for its plant type.
  3. Let the growth timer advance through stages.
  4. Right-click the mature crop to harvest.
  5. If replant_after_harvest is enabled, the crop resets to an early stage instead of disappearing.

docs.title: Crop Types At A Glance
docs.text:
• Lettuce is the simplest short ground crop.
  • Onion uses allium-style placement.
  • Corn is a tall crop and needs vertical room.
  • Tomato is a vine and needs a wall face.
  • Rice is aquatic and needs water above valid soil.

docs.title: Quality And Drops
docs.text: Harvest settings define normal drops, bonus drops, replanting, sounds, and quality chance. Fortune can improve configured bonus drops, and compatible custom enchantments can add effective Fortune or force replanting.

docs.title: Acquisition
docs.text: Survival access comes from grass drops, seed packets, chest loot, and natural patches. World generation and chest loot only affect new content, so old worlds may need starter items, seed packets, or admin seeding.

docs.title: Corn
docs.text: Corn field showing tall crop visuals. Field Value Item CORN Plant type TALL_PLANT Base growth 480 seconds Stages 5 Permission heirloom.crop.corn Replants yes

docs.title: Planting
docs.text:
Valid blocks: GRASS_BLOCK, DIRT, COARSE_DIRT, PODZOL, ROOTED_DIRT

Use the crop item on the correct block or face. If the crop has a permission, the player must have that node before planting.

docs.title: Harvest
docs.text:
Main drops: CORN 1-2.

If the crop keeps replant_after_harvest enabled, right-click harvest resets it to an early stage. Breaking the plant is treated as destruction, not a full harvest.

docs.title: Notes For Admins
docs.text: Edit this crop in crops.json or the relevant addon crop file. Growth scale, stage count, valid blocks, sounds, drop chances, quality chance, and permission nodes are all data-driven.

docs.title: EcoEnchants Integration
docs.text: Heirloom reads enchantment integration data from enchantment_integrations.json and resolves registered Bukkit enchantments by namespaced key.

docs.title: Bundled EcoEnchants Hooks
docs.text: Purpose Keys Behavior Force replant ecoenchants:replant, ecoenchants:replenish Crop resets after harvest even when it would normally be removed Fortune bonus ecoenchants:prospector Adds +1 effective Fortune per enchantment level

docs.title: How This Affects Players
docs.text: A replant enchantment makes farming smoother but still respects whether the crop is mature and harvestable. A Fortune bonus improves configured drop rolls; it does not invent drops that the crop JSON never defines.

docs.title: Server Owner Notes
docs.text: You can add other enchantment keys in the same namespace:name format. After editing, reload and harvest a mature test crop with the enchanted tool to confirm the integration is detected.

docs.title: Plant Types
docs.text:
Plant types define the physical block behavior behind a crop. Pick the type that matches how the crop should exist in the world, not only how the final display should look.

Type Used By Placement Practical Notes SHORT_PLANT Lettuce Ground plant on valid soil Best default for simple crops ALLIUM Onion Flower-style ground plant Useful for small vegetable visuals TALL_PLANT Corn Tall visual crop with vertical room Needs space above the base block ORCHARD_PINEAPPLE Mixology Pineapple Short fern on valid soil Upright fruit grows in the fern VINE Tomato, grapes Wall-attached vine Needs a face to attach to; poor fit for random flat patches AQUATIC Rice Soil under water Needs water setup and should be tested in claims BUSH Addon/extended crops Bush-style blocks Good for berry-like crops HANGING Addon/extended crops Ceiling-attached blocks Best for decorative or cave crops

Plant types are data-driven, but every type still depends on Minecraft block rules. If a crop uses a real plant block, protection plugins and physics can affect it.

docs.title: Seed Packets
docs.text:
Seed packets are custom items that roll weighted seeds when opened. They are useful when you want survival discovery without requiring every crop to drop from grass.

Packet Description Drops Weighted contents TEMPERATE_SEED_PACKET Contains seeds suited for temperate climates 3-6 LETTUCE (25), CORN (20), TOMATO (20), ONION (20), WHEAT_SEEDS (8), BEETROOT_SEEDS (4), CARROT (2), POTATO (1) TROPICAL_SEED_PACKET Contains seeds suited for tropical and exotic climates 3-5 RICE (40), MELON_SEEDS (20), PUMPKIN_SEEDS (20), COCOA_BEANS (15), BAMBOO (5)

Players open packets by using the item. If their inventory is full, extra seeds drop nearby.

docs.title: Design Advice
docs.text: Use seed packets for starter kits, market crates, quest rewards, and rare biome crops. Keep the drop count small if packets are common, otherwise a single packet can skip the early farming loop.
